npc:agathelos-the-raging.text: Agathelos the Raging. Deep within Razorfen Kraul, Agathelos the Raging is held among the thorned tunnels. The quilboar revere Agamaggan as their god and progenitor, and Agathelos’s great size carries spiritual meaning. His armor and fury make him one of the most dangerous beasts beneath the southern Barrens. Agamaggan, the titanic boar, is god and progenitor to the quilboar. So among the Razorfen tribes, a beast as large as Agathelos carries deep spiritual meaning. He stands roughly twice as tall as a Barrens thunder lizard. The quilboar keep Agathelos from roaming freely through the Kraul. Several guards maintain a field before the short, dead-end tunnel where he is penned. Intruders who break through that barrier face a raging beast, made more fearsome still by his fury.

npc:aggem-thorncurse.text: Aggem Thorncurse. In Razorfen Kraul, Aggem Thorncurse bears the title Death's Head Prophet. When threatened, he calls a boar spirit to his aid. Aggem guards part of Razorfen Kraul, where the Death's Head tribe dwells. His shamanic power lets him call a boar spirit into battle. The spirit reflects the quilboar's reverence for Agamaggan.

npc:aku-mai.text: Aku'mai. At Blackfathom Deeps, Aku'mai haunts the sunken temple of Elune along the Zoram Strand. An Old God's corruption tainted its sacred Moon Well, and Aku'mai rose from the waters as the Old God's servant. The Twilight's Hammer sacrifices innocents to Aku'mai for power. Blackfathom Deeps was once a great temple of Elune. Then an Old God's corruption tainted its sacred Moon Well, and Aku'mai rose from the waters. The gargantuan hydra serves the Old God. Now Aku'mai lairs in the drowned ruins of the night elves' temple, poisoning the waters along the Zoram Strand with its malice.

npc:arcanist-doan.text: Arcanist Doan. Within the Scarlet Monastery, Arcanist Doan guards the Athenaeum and its archives. A master human mage, he brings deadly arcane skill to the Scarlet Crusade. The Scarlet Crusade trusts martial fury and holy fervor. Doan believes arcane power is vital to driving the Scourge from Lordaeron. Deep in the Monastery's library, he keeps its lore and guards the Scarlet Key. That key secures Crusade sanctuaries across the northern kingdoms.

npc:baron-aquanis.text: Baron Aquanis. In the flooded Moonshrine Ruins of Blackfathom Deeps, Baron Aquanis rises from the depths when the Fathom Stone is disturbed. The Twilight's Hammer cultists occupy the ruins, and the Earthen Ring suspects the baron has been corrupted. Beneath the flooded halls of the Moonshrine Ruins lies the Fathom Stone, surrounded by Twilight's Hammer cultists. A fathom core rests within it. Read properly, the device reveals the history of nearby elemental activity. Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring sends Horde adventurers to recover it. Disturb the stone, and Baron Aquanis rises from the depths.

npc:baron-silverlaine.text: Baron Silverlaine. In the Great Hall above Pyrewood Village, Baron Silverlaine's spirit still lingers. He ruled Silverlaine Keep until Archmage Arugal unleashed worgen upon the region, and they slaughtered him. Baron Silverlaine ruled a noble estate in the southern hills of Silverpine. His fortress guarded the lands around it and kept them safe. Then Archmage Arugal summoned worgen to fight the rampaging Scourge and unleashed them upon the region. The feral beasts could not be controlled. They stormed the stronghold, overwhelmed its guards, and butchered the baron. Baron Silverlaine remains bound to the keep's ancient Great Hall. His restless ghost wanders among the wrecked dining tables where he once feasted. The cursed lord attacks intruders who enter his former home.

npc:bazil-thredd.text:
Bazil Thredd. In the eastern cell block, Bazil Thredd leads the Defias inmates in revolt. Edwin VanCleef's lieutenant has been held in the Stormwind Stockade since the Stonemasons' riots. Bazil Thredd stood beside Edwin VanCleef when the Stonemasons Guild rose against Stormwind's nobility. The guild had been denied payment for rebuilding the city, and VanCleef rejected the government's attempts to appease them. Open revolt followed.

Thredd served as his chief lieutenant and most trusted assistant. The city guard captured Thredd in the clashes that followed. VanCleef and the surviving masons fled to Westfall and formed the Defias Brotherhood. Thredd was sent to the Stormwind Stockade. A prison riot has overwhelmed the guards and opened the cells. Now the Stockade is an armed fortress beneath the Mage Quarter. Thredd commands the imprisoned Defias bandits, insurgents, and allied cutthroats from a post in the eastern wing. An ogre named Hamhock guards him. For years Thredd stayed silent behind bars, seemingly forsaken. Now Warden Thelwater wants him dead, hoping to break the rebellion's leadership before the chaos reaches the city streets.

npc:bazzalan.text: Bazzalan. Beneath Orgrimmar, Bazzalan directs the Searing Blade cult's work in Ragefire Chasm. He shares its leadership with Jergosh the Invoker. Bazzalan commands the Searing Blade's field forces in the lava caverns beneath Orgrimmar. While Thrall works to establish the Orcs' new home across Durotar, the satyr rogue moves through the winding caverns with twin blades, swift and lethal. From a volcanic ledge above the central chamber, Bazzalan watches over the cultist guards. Below him, Jergosh the Invoker conducts demonic rituals. Like all satyrs, Bazzalan's deepest loyalty belongs to demonic masters. He uses poison, quick strikes, and stealth against Horde scouts who venture near the cult's staging ground.

npc:blind-hunter.text: Blind Hunter. In the deepest reaches of Razorfen Kraul, the Blind Hunter roosts beyond the common bats. This pale albino bat prowls the quilboar redoubt, far from the cavern entrances. Razorfen Kraul winds through briars and dark caverns below ground. Common bats roost nearer the surface, where faint light reaches from outside. The Blind Hunter keeps to the furthest, darkest alcoves of the tangle. Its pale hide and milky gaze may come from generations spent apart from natural sunlight. The Blind Hunter is thought to have lost most or all of its ordinary sight. Scholars and scouts believe it tracks prey in the gloom with keen hearing and echolocation. It appears rarely, hunting only now and then among the dense thickets. For cavern explorers, a sighting of this phantom beast is rare.

npc:bloodmage-thalnos.text: Bloodmage Thalnos. In the Scarlet Monastery's Graveyard, Bloodmage Thalnos haunts the tombs, hungry for vengeance. The plague of undeath claimed him, and he remains deep within the Crusade's holy grounds. No record tells who Thalnos was in life. The plague of undeath claimed him, and he rose as a withered skeleton. Still, he clings to fiery magic and arcane mastery. He cries out for vengeance and more souls. From the deepest corner of the monastery's courtyard tombs, Thalnos commands apparitions and shambling undead minions. He attacks anyone who disturbs his domain. Beneath the Crusade's sacred halls, his presence is a bitter contradiction. He embodies the horror they swore to eradicate.

npc:bruegal-ironknuckle.text: Bruegal Ironknuckle. In the Stormwind Stockade, Bruegal Ironknuckle prowls the halls during an open revolt. The dangerous dwarf is a powerful brawler, and anyone trying to restore order may face his fists. Bruegal Ironknuckle prowls the Stormwind Stockade during its open revolt. The dwarf is known for his brutal strength in a brawl. Many of the city's most volatile cutthroats have seized the underground cellblocks, and Bruegal is among them. He leaves his cell and roams the halls, ready to bash anyone trying to quell the uprising. Bruegal Ironknuckle is among the rogues and outlaws held deep beneath Stormwind. The Defias Brotherhood and its ringleaders direct much of the revolt, while inmates like Bruegal show that the prison holds criminals from across the eastern realms. No record here tells what crimes brought him there. His fierce resilience makes him elusive and one of the deadliest lone inmates in the corridors.

npc:captain-greenskin.text: Captain Greenskin. In the Deadmines cove, Captain Greenskin readies a warship for Edwin VanCleef. The goblin pirate directs its crew and construction for the Defias Brotherhood, preparing the ironclad juggernaut to sail against Stormwind. Captain Greenskin paces the main deck of the juggernaut under construction in the Deadmines cove. A seasoned goblin mariner, he joined Edwin VanCleef's inner circle to turn an underground cavern into a drydock for a warship. Captain Greenskin commands cutthroats, not stonemasons or bandits. His crew includes Mr. Smite, his fearsome tauren first mate, and Cookie, the murloc ship's cook. Together, they hold the gangplanks and upper deck, guarding the way to VanCleef's private cabin atop the bridge.

npc:charlga-razorflank.text: Charlga Razorflank. In Razorfen Kraul, Charlga Razorflank leads the Razorfen quilboar. They drove the tauren from the southern Barrens, claiming to fight for their fallen god, Agamaggan. Charlga Razorflank rules from the tangled brambles of Razorfen Kraul. Her people honor her as a master geomancer, and none among the quilboar can equal her experimental magic. She bound her fractious kin into a deadly force. With primal earth and giant thorns grown from the remains of Agamaggan, the fallen demigod, Charlga shaped the Kraul into a fortress few can enter.

npc:commander-springvale.text: Commander Springvale. At Shadowfang Keep, Commander Springvale's spirit still guards the halls where he fell. Once a devoted paladin and commander, he was slain with his men by Arugal's worgen and now haunts the castle. Commander Springvale led the garrison at Shadowfang Keep in Silverpine Forest. Before the keep fell into ruin, he was an honorable paladin devoted to the Holy Light. After Lordaeron fell to the Scourge, he kept watch over the fortress through those troubled days. Archmage Arugal summoned worgen from beyond this world to strengthen Dalaran's failing ranks against the undead Scourge. The wild beasts soon escaped his control and descended on Shadowfang Keep. They slaughtered Baron Silverlaine and his entire guard. Springvale died in the halls he had sworn to protect, his service cut short. Death did not release Springvale. His ghost haunts the keep's council room alongside spectral soldiers. He still wields paladin powers against intruders, including Holy Light and Hammer of Justice.

npc:cookie.text: Cookie. Beneath the juggernaut in the Deadmines, Cookie tends the crew's cauldrons. A murloc in the Defias Brotherhood, he cooks under Captain Greenskin and Edwin VanCleef. In the underground dry dock, his post is the only one a visitor may pass by. Cookie cooks beneath the decks of the juggernaut at Ironclad Cove. No human outrider or goblin engineer takes the duty; the solitary murloc does. No one knows how he came to hold the post. The crew may doubt a murloc's cooking, but pirates rarely choose their meals with care. In Moonbrook's underworld, a meal is a meal. Cookie patrols the waterways and shores around the pirate flagship. He fights with cooking utensils and throws acidic brews. Though apart from typical murloc tribes, he defends his cauldron with savage force, hurling caustic mixtures at intruders in the docks. His station lies away from the main gangplanks, so many who storm the cove pass his kitchen by. Cookie is the only overseer aboard the Defias juggernaut who can be bypassed.

npc:dark-iron-ambassador.text: Dark Iron Ambassador. Deep in Gnomeregan, the Dark Iron Ambassador moves among the ruined halls as an envoy of his clan. Why the clan has come to the fallen gnome capital remains unclear. In Gnomeregan’s irradiated halls, the Dark Iron Ambassador speaks for his clan. The purpose of his mission is unknown.

npc:dextren-ward.text:
Dextren Ward. In the Stormwind Stockade, Dextren Ward remains a prisoner during a bloody uprising. Before his capture, he dug up bodies at Raven Hill Cemetery in Duskwood and sold them to the necromancer Morbent Fel. Darkshire's town council has marked him for death. Before chains bound him beneath Stormwind, Dextren Ward robbed graves in Duskwood for profit. At Raven Hill Cemetery, he dug up the newly buried dead. He sold the bodies to local practitioners of dark arts. Morbent Fel, a necromancer, was Ward's main customer. His rituals plagued Duskwood and swelled the undead ranks. By supplying him with bodies, Ward helped spread terror through Darkshire.

Stormwind authorities eventually captured Ward and brought him to the Stockade. The people of Duskwood demanded justice for his crimes. Councilman Millstipe called for Ward's hand as proof. A rebellion swept through the Stockade, and Ward was freed from his cell in the chaos. Armed and vicious, he seized control of his corner of the prison. Now he uses fear to keep intruders away. Alliance forces seeking to restore order count him among their priority targets.

npc:edwin-vancleef.text:
Edwin VanCleef. In the Deadmines, Edwin VanCleef commands the Defias Brotherhood. He once led the Stonemasons who rebuilt Stormwind City after the Second War. The House of Nobles denied the workers their promised pay, and VanCleef now seeks vengeance against the kingdom he helped restore. Edwin VanCleef led the Stonemasons Guild in rebuilding Stormwind City after the First War. A peerless craftsman and idealist, he mastered architecture and directed the work on the capital's grand ramparts and towering cathedrals. His childhood friend Mathias Shaw taught him stealth, subterfuge, thievery, and bladecraft. VanCleef became a deadly operative as well as a master architect. After years of labor, the Stonemasons finished rebuilding Stormwind. The House of Nobles had run up great debts through military campaigns and refused the guild its promised pay. VanCleef demanded restitution, but the nobles dissolved the guild.

He led the workers in a riot and out of the city. In the chaos, his lieutenant and most trusted assistant, Bazil Thredd, was captured and left in the Stockade. In Westfall, VanCleef gathered the exiled workers and allied outcasts beneath the Defias Brotherhood's banner.

npc:electrocutioner-6000.text: Electrocutioner 6000. In Gnomeregan's Launch Bay, Electrocutioner 6000 guards the upper platform. The spider tank fights for Mekgineer Thermaplugg and the irradiated leper gnomes who follow him. After Gnomeregan fell, Mekgineer Thermaplugg and the irradiated leper gnomes who follow him took control of the city's war machines. Electrocutioner 6000 guards the Launch Bay's upper platform. It strikes intruders with high-voltage current. Electrocutioner 6000 guards the Workshop Key, which opens Gnomeregan's back door into its workshops. Bring down the machine, and the key gives you a quicker route into the city's depths.

npc:fenrus-the-devourer.text: Fenrus the Devourer. In Shadowfang Keep, Fenrus the Devourer guards Archmage Arugal's upper sanctum. The enormous worg is the archmage's pet, swollen by unnatural magic. Anyone seeking Arugal's study must face beast and master. Fenrus the Devourer prowls outside Archmage Arugal's private chambers, deep within Shadowfang Keep. The worg is no rampart worgen. Swollen to enormous size, Fenrus stalks among the shelves, scrolls, and arcane tools in Arugal's study. The archmage keeps the beast as both pet and guard against anyone who comes seeking his head. Dark magic has saturated Shadowfang Keep since Baron Silverlaine's downfall, and Fenrus bears its mark. Archmage Arugal or his unleashed worgen warped the native predator through arcane or shadowy experiments. Now Fenrus is a ravenous juggernaut, so feral and bound by magic that no hunter can charm or tame him.

npc:gelihast.text: Gelihast. Within Blackfathom Deeps, Gelihast guards an altar in the flooded Pool of Ask'ar. His Blindlight murlocs gather around him in the sunken temple. Deep beneath the Zoram Strand, Gelihast has made his lair in Blackfathom Deeps. Most murlocs keep to the coastal shallows, but he strikes intruders with twin swords. He moves too quickly for many to react, and casters who come within his reach rarely survive. Gelihast rules the Pool of Ask'ar with his Blindlight brood. At the first sign of trouble, they swarm to his side. Beyond his lair stands an altar. Those who defeat him and touch it receive the Blessing of Blackfathom.

npc:ghamoo-ra-classic.text: Ghamoo-ra. In Blackfathom Deeps, Ghamoo-ra guards a small island in the Pool of Ask'ar. The ancient giant turtle tramples anyone who draws near. Blackfathom Deeps was once a night elven temple to Elune. Now flooded, its ruins belong to naga, satyr, and the nihilistic Twilight's Hammer cult. Ghamoo-ra dwells among them, his enormous, thick shell turning aside all but the strongest blows. Lesser turtles gather around Ghamoo-ra on a small island in the Pool of Ask'ar, yet they leave travelers alone. Ghamoo-ra attacks anyone who comes near. Beneath his trampling bulk, they are crushed.

npc:gilnid.text: Gilnid. Deep in the Deadmines, Gilnid directs the Defias Brotherhood's goblin forges. Known as the Smelter, he oversees the work that turns raw ore into refined metal and munitions for Edwin VanCleef's hidden ironclad juggernaut. His foundry produces the heavy cannons the Brotherhood needs to strike Stormwind. Deep in the Deadmines, the Defias Brotherhood relies on the foundry for weapons of war. Gilnid, VanCleef's head smelter, commands goblin laborers, tinkers, and smiths there. Taller than most of his kin, he drives them through smoke and slag, barking orders and allowing no breaks. Their work turns raw iron ore into heavy plating and deadly ordnance.

npc:hamhock.text: Hamhock. In the Stormwind Stockade, Hamhock remains among the rioting prisoners. The massive two-headed ogre is one of the prison’s most brutal inmates. Hamhock is a towering two-headed ogre held in the Stormwind Stockade. The prison was built for petty thieves, murderers, and political dissidents. So his size makes him a fearsome presence among the cells. When prisoners seized control, Hamhock remained amid the disorder and crushed anyone who entered his cellblock. No record tells how Hamhock was captured or why he was locked among Stormwind’s thieves and dissidents. Whatever brought him to the Stockade, he is now one of its most dangerous inmates.

npc:herod.text: Herod. In the Scarlet Monastery's Armory, Herod trains the Crusade's melee fighters. A renowned champion, he commands the Armory and wages the Crusade's holy war with fierce skill and zeal. Alliance dissidents and the Horde's rulers in Undercity seek his death to weaken the order. Herod commands the Armory within the Scarlet Monastery. Unlike the spellcasters and paladins in the Cathedral, he relies on physical strength. Clad in mail and bearing a massive two-handed axe, he trains cohorts of Scarlet Trainees. He teaches them to fight with fury and destroy anyone beyond the Crusade's cause. Herod oversees the weapons and combat training of the Crusade's front-line warriors. Raleigh the Devout, an ex-Crusader disillusioned with the order's madness, lives in Southshore and calls for Herod's death to break its military leadership. In the Undercity, the dreadlord Varimathras also seeks Herod's execution. He wants the dangerous human stronghold cleared from the border of Forsaken territory.

npc:high-inquisitor-fairbanks.text: High Inquisitor Fairbanks. In the Scarlet Crusade, High Inquisitor Fairbanks's fate remains bound to the order's dark descent. Before Lordaeron fell, he was a revered priest and a trusted advisor to Highlord Alexandros Mograine. Before Lordaeron fell, Fairbanks was a respected priest of the Knights of the Silver Hand. Highlord Alexandros Mograine trusted him above all others. Mograine bore the Ashbringer. Fairbanks stood beside Mograine, High General Abbendis and Grand Inquisitor Isillien when they founded the Scarlet Crusade, an order sworn to destroy the Scourge.

npc:houndmaster-loksey.text: Houndmaster Loksey. In the Scarlet Monastery's Library wing, Houndmaster Loksey keeps the Crusade's war dogs ready. He breeds and trains them to hunt undead, intruders, and those the Crusade judges heretics. His harsh discipline has made the Monastery's beasts feared across Tirisfal Glades. Houndmaster Loksey trains vicious dogs to track and attack. The Scarlet Crusade sends them to sniff out plague-tainted corpses, uncover hidden infiltrators, and run down survivors fleeing the zealots' wrath. Loksey commands the hounds guarding the Library wing. They stand ready to tear intruders limb from limb. Loksey's brother, Huntsman Leopold, serves the Scarlet Crusade as its envoy to the Argent Dawn at Light's Hope Chapel. In private, Leopold thinks Loksey can barely manage his hounds, let alone handle high-stakes diplomacy. Yet Loksey remains a key officer in the Monastery's inner hierarchy.

npc:interrogator-vishas.text:
Interrogator Vishas. Deep in the Scarlet Monastery, Interrogator Vishas has captives at his mercy. The Scarlet Crusade’s master of torment takes pleasure in breaking prisoners and testing mortal flesh. In the Scarlet Monastery’s crypts and burial grounds, Interrogator Vishas tends the Crusade’s captives. Outside, zealots march in gleaming armor beneath banners of purity. Inside, Vishas reveals the cruelty behind their righteous fury.

Interrogation serves the Crusade’s need for intelligence, and Vishas prizes it as a craft. He revels in the agony of Forsaken captives, captured Scourge, and living travelers branded heretics.

npc:jergosh-the-invoker.text: Jergosh the Invoker. Beneath Orgrimmar, Jergosh the Invoker leads a cult against the Horde. In Ragefire Chasm, he turns to demonic arts while Thrall guides the orcs toward honor and shamanism. Jergosh gathers the Searing Blade beneath Orgrimmar. Thrall leads the orcs toward honor and shamanism, but Jergosh turns to demonic power. In Ragefire Chasm, he draws followers into a sect aligned with the remnants of the Shadow Council. From beneath the Horde capital, the cult works against the path the new Horde has chosen.

npc:kam-deepfury.text: Kam Deepfury. In Stormwind's Stockade, Kam Deepfury waits apart from the Defias rebels. Captured after arranging the blast that shattered the Thandol Span far to the north, the Dark Iron dwarf is held far from his kin. Kam Deepfury is a Dark Iron dwarf held deep in the Stormwind Stockade. Most prisoners there are disgruntled Stonemasons or Defias rebels, but he is neither. Captured after an operation crippled vital northern infrastructure, he remains cut off from his kin beneath Blackrock Mountain. Like the rebels sharing the corridors, he is hostile to the Alliance. Alliance intelligence at Dun Modr, near the Wetlands' northern border, named Kam Deepfury as the chief architect of the blast that shattered the Thandol Span. The explosion severed one of the massive stone bridges between the Wetlands and the Arathi Highlands. It crippled a vital trade and military route for Ironforge and the Alliance. It also killed a kin of Longbraid the Grim, the dwarf commander.

npc:lady-anacondra.text: Lady Anacondra. Deep in the Wailing Caverns, Lady Anacondra holds to the Druids of the Fang. She followed Naralex in his effort to heal the Barrens, but his communion with the Emerald Dream became a nightmare. It shattered her mind and turned her devotion toward remaking the land in the dream’s image. Lady Anacondra followed Naralex into the caverns as he sought the Barrens’ subterranean springs through the Emerald Dream. Then dark visions seized his mind, and the nightmare spread from the dreaming realm to his disciples. Her sanity broke. Her hope for the land became a cold, reptilian obsession. Lady Anacondra guards the Wailing Caverns’ first chambers. She and the other Fanglords have cast aside the Cenarion Circle’s teachings and embraced the viper’s vicious ways. She wields lightning and nature magic, and keeps Naralex in his twisted sleep with slumbering trances. Above, the nightmare’s corruption still threatens the Barrens.

npc:lady-sarevess.text: Lady Sarevess. In Blackfathom Deeps, Lady Sarevess works dark sorceries among the flooded ruins. Lady Sarevess performs rituals in a flooded grotto within the Pool of Ask'ar. The Twilight's Hammer cultists haunt the sunken temple as well. They pursue their own worship deeper in the cavern. Lady Sarevess commands elemental currents and crackling lightning. Loyal naga sentinels and summoned water elementals guard her sanctuary. She fights intruders who threaten her dark work.

npc:lord-cobrahn.text: Lord Cobrahn. Deep in the Wailing Caverns, Lord Cobrahn commands the corrupted Druids of the Fang. He was a night elf druid in Naralex's order, until the nightmare in the cavern springs claimed him. Now he guards the twisted labyrinth in a deadly serpent guise. Lord Cobrahn once served Naralex in his druid order. When Naralex entered the Wailing Caverns beneath the Barrens, he hoped to draw upon the underground springs and restore life to the arid wastes. Cobrahn went with him. But Naralex's communion with the Emerald Dream decayed into a twisting nightmare, and Cobrahn's mind shattered with those of his brothers. The nightmare warped Cobrahn's shapeshifting into a predatory reptilian form unlike the totemic beasts of Cenarion tradition. In battle, he takes the guise of a deadly serpent. Venomous deviate pythons flank him, and a vicious claw marks his right hand. Cobrahn rules his part of the grottos and violently purges anyone who tries to break the nightmare's hold on the caverns.

npc:lord-pythas.text:
Lord Pythas. Deep in the Wailing Caverns, Lord Pythas guards Naralex's slumber. Once a night elf warrior in Naralex's personal guard, he now leads the corrupted Druids of the Fang. His skill in battle and serpent magic bar the way to his master. Pythas joined Naralex's personal guard when the druid's expedition entered the Barrens' dry wastes. A seasoned night elf warrior, he studied druidism to help Naralex restore life to the arid realm. Yet discipline and valor could not shield him from the corruption hidden in the caverns' depths. Dark nightmares seized Naralex's connection to the Emerald Dream. Pythas and his fellow acolytes fell under their sway. He forsook his old loyalty and became a leader of the Druids of the Fang.

Some serpent lords favor spells or beast forms. Pythas wields nature magic alongside deadly combat skill. Now he prowls the winding caverns and guards the nightmare's hold on the spring.

npc:lord-serpentis.text: Lord Serpentis. Deep in the Wailing Caverns, Lord Serpentis leads the Druids of the Fang. Once a mighty druid in Naralex's order, he fell to madness when Naralex's dream soured in the cavern springs. Now he helps command the serpent-worshipping sect near the corrupted Naralex, who lies slumbering. Before the cavern springs darkened, Serpentis held great power and prestige as a druid. He belonged to the noble order led by Naralex. Together, they hoped to heal the Barrens with the springs and the Emerald Dream. But Naralex's vision became a corrupting nightmare, and its rising madness took hold of Serpentis and the other druids. Naralex's twisted dreams spread corruption through his followers. Serpentis and the others became the Druids of the Fang, abandoning Cenarion balance and the totem animals of old. Now they seek to remake the Barrens in the image of their twisted dreams instead of healing it. Serpentis shares leadership with Lady Anacondra, Lord Cobrahn and Lord Pythas.

npc:lorgus-jett.text: Lorgus Jett. In Blackfathom Deeps, Lorgus Jett leads the Twilight's Hammer through flooded ruins. The Horde has marked him as a target. Among the Twilight's Hammer in Blackfathom Deeps, Lorgus Jett is a human. Many cultists there are orcs or tauren, but Jett ranges from the upper Moonshrine Ruins to the tunnels beyond Gelihast, the murloc defiler. He directs the cult's rituals and violent ambitions in the ancient night elf ruins.

npc:miner-johnson.text: Miner Johnson. Deep in the Deadmines, Miner Johnson oversees the digging as a seasoned miner. He works ahead of the heavy machinery, though he appears only now and then. Miner Johnson digs with the laborers beneath the Deadmines, where they work on Edwin VanCleef's hidden fortress. Before the shredders in the Mast Room, he waits in an alcove to the left. He is stronger and more aggressive than the other miners. Since he wanders the tunnels, he can be hard to find. Beneath Moonbrook, the Defias Brotherhood needs ore for weapons, reinforced shafts, and mechanical contraptions. Johnson and the other miners dig the mineral seams beneath Westfall. Anyone who enters his work area finds that he guards it fiercely.

npc:mr-smite.text: Mr. Smite. At Ironclad Cove, Mr. Smite guards the Defias ship and its crew. The tauren serves Captain Greenskin as first mate and watches the docks where Edwin VanCleef's dreadnaught is being fitted out. Intruders meet his great strength and a changing array of weapons. At Ironclad Cove, Mr. Smite keeps order on the docks as first mate to the goblin Captain Greenskin. Most of the Defias Brotherhood are disaffected humans and goblin tinkerers, but Smite is a battle-hardened tauren from far beyond Kalimdor's plains. He commands a rowdy pirate crew as they fit out Edwin VanCleef's secret dreadnaught. No one may disrupt their work. Mr. Smite is a showman and a versatile weaponmaster, not just a fighter of brute force. He toys with challengers and draws out the fight, leaving them a false hope of victory. When pressed, he stamps the ground hard enough to stun his foes, then searches a nearby chest for another weapon. First comes a quick dueling blade, then twin cleaving reavers, and at last a huge two-handed warhammer.

npc:mutanus-the-devourer.text: Mutanus the Devourer. In the Wailing Caverns, Mutanus the Devourer haunts Naralex's sleeping mind as a pale, monstrous murloc. The creature emerged from the Emerald Nightmare, and must fall before Naralex can awaken. Naralex, a night elf druid, sought to restore the Barrens by joining its underground springs to the Emerald Dream. Instead, the Emerald Nightmare entered his thoughts. Trapped in an agonizing vision, Naralex's fears took shape through the corruption as an immense, albino murloc.

npc:naralex.text: Naralex. Beneath the Barrens, Naralex sleeps while his dream of green turns to nightmare. The night elf druid sought to restore the parched land through the Emerald Dream, but corruption overtook his slumber and twisted his followers into venomous fiends. Naralex came to the Barrens with devoted disciples, hoping to restore the forest that covered the plains before the Great Sundering. Beneath the savannah, he found underground springs and rushing geysers. He named the caverns for the howling wind and steam that moaned through the rock. He believed a deep trance could channel the Emerald Dream into those waters, carrying life to the surface and making the wasteland bloom. Deep in the caverns, Naralex entered meditation and reached toward the Emerald Dream. Corruption ensnared his mind instead of the peaceful wild nature he sought. The Emerald Nightmare seized the sleeping druid and made him a conduit for dark energies to enter the living world. Springs turned foul, fungal blooms mutated, and the caverns' beasts became ravenous horrors.

npc:oggleflint.text: Oggleflint. In Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar, Oggleflint leads his trogg tribe toward the surface. Near the cavern entrance, he commands his pack as they threaten the Horde capital above. Deep beneath Orgrimmar, Oggleflint and his troggs climbed from fiery tunnels into Ragefire Chasm. Among the molten rock, they carved out a primitive domain and defend it with brutal force. The troggs have little advanced civilization. Oggleflint rules his pack through sheer strength. Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem sent diplomats into the chasm to make peace with the troggs. The troggs turned on them and killed them. Maur Grimtotem, one of the envoys, lies dead in the caverns under Oggleflint’s watch. Near the cavern entrance, Oggleflint waits to strike at outsiders who venture into the dark. Oggleflint’s tribe lives directly beneath Thrall’s capital, a hazard the Horde cannot tolerate. The troggs creep closer to the surface. Their volatile nature threatens to carry them into the Drag and Cleft of Shadow if left undisturbed.

npc:old-serra-kis.text: Old Serra'kis. In the flooded depths beneath the Moonshrine Sanctum, Old Serra'kis waits in Blackfathom Deeps. The enormous threshadon hides in a submerged cave, deadly to anyone who seeks him there. The Twilight's Hammer has made its home in the sunken Moonshrine Ruins. Beneath the Moonshrine Sanctum, dark waters hide older and wilder things. Old Serra'kis, the largest threshadon in the sunken temple, lurks in the Forgotten Pool. Few would think to look in that flooded cave beneath the ruins. You must dive beneath the temple floor to reach Old Serra'kis in the flooded cavern. No air pockets break the water, and the cave is as deadly as the beast within. Cornered in the murk, Serra'kis shows an unnatural resilience. He drains life from his attackers with shadow energy and sustains his own vitality in the darkness.

npc:overlord-ramtusk.text: Overlord Ramtusk. Deep in Razorfen Kraul, Overlord Ramtusk rallies the quilboar warriors for battle. He calls for victory and for Agamaggan, and his fall breaks the defenders’ martial strength. Overlord Ramtusk commands the quilboar stronghold deep in Razorfen Kraul, in the southern Barrens. He enters battle crying out to Agamaggan, the boar demigod, and rules the Kraul’s fighters with unyielding authority. Ramtusk directs the quilboar warriors through the Kraul’s winding brambles. He keeps tight discipline among the bristled fighters who defend their tribe’s sanctum. Elite marksmen flank him as he fights on the front line, bellowing rallying shouts and unleashing slams that can break opposing battle lines in seconds.

npc:rhahk-zor.text: Rhahk'Zor. In the Deadmines, Rhahk'Zor drives the work forward by force. As head foreman, he keeps Defias laborers and miners in line while they build Edwin VanCleef's underground fortress. The Defias Brotherhood has made an underground fortress of Moonbrook's abandoned gold mines. Rhahk'Zor was appointed head foreman to direct the work. He oversees the crews and laborers as they carve tunnels and build VanCleef's secret projects. Rhahk'Zor keeps order with his strength and an immense stone-headed hammer. Defias diggers and goblin engineers know the towering foreman may strike a crushing blow if they defy him or fall behind schedule.

npc:scarlet-commander-mograine.text: Scarlet Commander Mograine. Within the Scarlet Monastery, Scarlet Commander Mograine guards the Cathedral with the Scarlet Crusade. A zealous paladin, he faces efforts by the Horde and Alliance to disrupt the Crusade's threat to Tirisfal Glades and the lands around it. At the heart of the Scarlet Monastery, Scarlet Commander Mograine leads the Scarlet Crusade garrison in the Crusader's Chapel. A devoted paladin, he strikes with holy power and shields himself. Those the Crusade judges corrupted or unclean meet his stunning blows.

npc:sneed.text: Sneed. Deep in the Deadmines, Sneed directs the Defias Brotherhood’s timber work. From the Mast Room, he pilots a heavy shredder of his own design, cutting lumber for Edwin VanCleef’s secret juggernaut. The Defias Brotherhood draws most of its members from human stonemasons and laborers. Yet Edwin VanCleef brought Sneed in for his engineering skill and ruthless efficiency. A warship needs skilled trades, and Sneed directs the timber work in the Mast Room beside the underground rail network. There, wood is felled, cut, and shaped for VanCleef’s colossal dreadnaught. Sneed cares about costs and quotas, whatever the consequences. From a custom shredder fitted with oversized buzz saws, he directs the work. Its blades turn raw trunks into shipbuilding timber in seconds. When intruders corner him, Sneed uses the machine’s armor to grind them down. If the shredder fails, he scrambles from the wreckage and fights barehanded.

npc:sneed-s-shredder.text: Sneed's Shredder. Deep in the Deadmines, Sneed pilots a lumber machine for Edwin VanCleef's shipwrights. Its blades cut timber and meet intruders with armored force. In the Deadmines foundry, goblin shredders cut timber for Edwin VanCleef's hidden juggernaut. They also turn their armored force against intruders. Sneed oversees the lumber works and pilots this modified machine himself. Its oversized buzzsaw is a weapon of defense. Sneed rides above the spinning blades in an open cockpit, behind heavy iron plating. The shredder's clatter can scatter his foes. When the machine breaks down in a burst of sparks, Sneed leaps from the wreckage and fights on.

npc:taragaman-the-hungerer.text: Taragaman the Hungerer. Beneath Orgrimmar, Taragaman the Hungerer prowls Ragefire Chasm and threatens the city above. The Horde seeks his death to end the demonic taint below its capital. Taragaman the Hungerer prowls among Ragefire Chasm's magma pools, threatening Orgrimmar. Scouts and young warriors sent into the dark caverns see the demonic felguard as the Searing Blade cult's leader. With infernal strength, he bends the weak-willed and corrupts the passages beneath Thrall's fortress.

npc:targorr-the-dread.text: Targorr the Dread. In the Stormwind Stockade, Targorr the Dread waits among rioting convicts. Corruption and neglect delayed his execution, and the Defias uprising opened a way out. Before his capture, Targorr the Dread served Warlord Gath'Ilzogg as the Blackrock clan's supreme executioner. From the occupied ruins in Redridge, he tormented Stormwind guards and militiamen defending the borderlands. His cruelty surpassed even the Dark Horde's violence, and few names were more reviled across the kingdom. Alliance forces captured Targorr alive and brought him in chains to the capital. They locked him in the high-security Stockade, but Stormwind's courts stalled over his execution. Graft, endless paperwork, and neglect kept the courts from delivering the death sentence he had earned. So a bloodthirsty war criminal remained in a cell beneath the heart of the city. When the Defias Brotherhood broke prisoners out by force, Targorr seized his chance. He escaped his cell and joined the Defias rioters, turning his cellblock into a slaughterhouse. Warden Thelwater has lost control of the prison. Lakeshire still bears the wounds Targorr dealt its defenders, and seeks adventurers willing to enter the riot and bring back the butcher's head.

npc:twilight-lord-kelris.text: Twilight Lord Kelris. At Blackfathom Deeps, Twilight Lord Kelris leads the Twilight's Hammer from the sunken ruins. The orc warlock holds high rank in the cult and directs its rites in the Moonshrine Sanctum. There, his followers worship Aku'mai and seek a reign of cosmic chaos. Twilight Lord Kelris directs the cultists who seized the sunken ruins of Blackfathom Deeps. For years, he slipped past watchful eyes in Darnassus and evaded the Argent Dawn. Whenever ancient malice stirred across Kalimdor, Kelris was suspected of being behind it. He pledged himself to the Old Gods, not to warlords or clans. He seeks to unmake mortal civilization and return Azeroth to primordial chaos. In the Moonshrine Sanctum, Kelris oversees the cult's worship of Aku'mai, a vicious three-headed hydra who serves an Old God. Allied with the naga, the Twilight's Hammer occupies the drowned temple. Kelris leads the cult's rites and sacrifices innocents to Aku'mai in exchange for power.

npc:verdan-the-everliving.text: Verdan the Everliving. In the Wailing Caverns, Verdan the Everliving lurks in deep tunnels and attacks those who enter. He dwells near the sleeping druid Naralex and the Druids of the Fang. Verdan is the largest bog beast in the overgrown depths of the Wailing Caverns. He is an elemental of foliage, silt, and mire, haunting its flooded hollows. Nothing is known of him from before corruption reached the caverns.

npc:viscous-fallout.text: Viscous Fallout. In Gnomeregan's lower passages, Viscous Fallout drifts through the toxic runoff. Radiation flooded Gnomeregan after Mekgineer Thermaplugg advised a treacherous plan to wipe out the invading troggs. The fallout filled the city's lower levels with toxic slime and contamination. Viscous Fallout is a water elemental, its substance thick with the city's toxic waste. Its origins before the fall are unknown. Viscous Fallout drifts through Gnomeregan's irradiated lower passages as a living pool of toxic sludge. It spews volleys of toxin, then lashes out at anything in its path. Those who enter the city to cleanse its tainted depths must destroy the creature.

subzone:camp-narache.text: Camp Narache. Camp Narache is where young tauren begin their training, high on Red Cloud Mesa in southern Mulgore. It is the ancestral home of the Hawkwind tribe. Up here, above the plains, the old traditions are kept. But the camp must always stand guard, against the quilboar and the centaur. The camp stands at the northern edge of the mesa, a village of great hide lodges and pavilions. There is a tent for wounded braves, and a lodge for speaking with the ancestors. At its center, the tribal elders and trainers stand in a circle. Among them is the venerable Greatmother Hawkwind. She still guides the young, as they take up their place as defenders of the Earth Mother. The sheer cliffs of the mesa make a natural fortress, yet the camp knows little peace. Bristleback quilboar press in from Brambleblade Ravine, and centaur scouts linger in the distance. Here young hunters, shaman, druids and warriors prove their mettle. They cull the angry wildlife, guard the village well and turn back the quilboar raiders. Then they walk the great path down, into the wider valleys of Mulgore.

subzone:coldridge-valley.text: Coldridge Valley. Coldridge Valley is where young dwarves and gnome refugees train to serve Ironforge. Snow lies deep over this sheltered vale, high in the southwest of Dun Morogh. Sheer cliffs close it in. Only one road leads out to the wider mountains, and that is Coldridge Pass. The recruits gather at Anvilmar, the valley's training hall. There they learn to fight, to move unseen and to wield sorcery. Veteran dwarves teach them, side by side with gnome scholars who have lost their home. Out on the snowy valley floor roam boars and hungry winter wolves. They test whether a novice can survive the frontier. But this valley is not at peace. Frostmane trolls camp here, at Frostmane Hovel and beyond. They say the land was theirs by ancestral right, and they skirmish with the mountaineers over it. And Rockjaw troggs have overrun Coldridge Pass. It is the tunnel to Kharanos, and while it is blocked, nothing moves freely to Ironforge.

subzone:deathknell.text:
Deathknell. Deathknell is where the newly freed dead first wake, in a hidden valley of southwestern Tirisfal. They have broken from the Lich King's grasp, and here they join the Forsaken. But mindless Scourge, zealots and wild beasts beset the village. For anyone who would claim a place in Sylvanas Windrunner's kingdom, it is a harsh first trial. The valley lies behind jagged hills, just north of the Silverpine border. Elite Deathguards keep the narrow gorge out of the valley sealed. Most towns in Tirisfal kept their human names from fallen Lordaeron. This one did not. The undead who claimed it named it Deathknell.

The town itself is split in two. Its northern half is still overrun by mindless zombies and feral ghouls, the village forge with it. The Forsaken cling to the southern grounds, around the old church. There the caretakers take in each new arrival, and bring them into the Banshee Queen's service. Survival here is never certain. To the northwest, monstrous spiders have taken Night Web's Hollow, a gold mine the young Forsaken nation needs. To the southeast, the Scarlet Crusade keeps a camp, and watches the valley without rest. Its couriers run to the Crusade's strongholds in the east, and its scouts probe Deathknell's defenses. And in the northern ruins, the caretakers must still fight off the mindless dead.

subzone:northshire-abbey.text:
Northshire Abbey. Northshire Abbey trains the kingdom's newest defenders, in the foothills of Northshire Valley. It is the spiritual heart of the Brotherhood of Northshire. And for those who answer Stormwind's call, few schools in the land are finer. It has been built twice. Centuries ago, clerics came south from Lordaeron to spread the Holy Light. They founded the Holy Order of Northshire Clerics, and they built its abbey. It soon became part of the life of the kingdom, caring for its sick. For years it tended the young Guardian Medivh, while he lay in his long coma.

Then the First War came. Brigands and the Horde struck at the abbey again and again, until it lay in ruins. In the Second War, the Alliance of Lordaeron freed the region. Afterward, Archbishop Alonsus Faol helped to raise the abbey anew. And he refounded its protectors as the Brotherhood of Northshire. Today the abbey takes in volunteers, militia recruits and novices, all of them hoping to defend Stormwind. In its halls, instructors teach the martial, arcane and holy arts. Scouts and rogues train out in the yards. And the Knights of the Silver Hand keep watch over it all.

But the peace here is fragile. Kobolds have overrun the nearby mines, and wolves prowl the orchards. Agents of the Defias Brotherhood stalk the valley roads. Not even the abbey's archives are safe from them. They steal its ancient scrolls and sacred librams.

subzone:sen-jin-village.text:
Sen'jin Village. Sen'jin Village shelters the Darkspear on Durotar's southern shore. Vol'jin led them there after Zalazane seized the Echo Isles, and gave the refuge his fallen father's name. Across the shallows, their lost home waits. The Darkspear survivors have made their refuge on Durotar's shore. After Zalazane betrayed the tribe and seized the Echo Isles, Chieftain Vol'jin led them across the strait to the mainland. They raised crude huts beneath coastal cliffs, with the water and their lost home in view.

The village bears the name of Sen'jin, Vol'jin's father. Murlocs captured and sacrificed him during the Third War. Though the Darkspear are closely allied with Thrall's Horde, exile remains their burden. The lost isles lie just across the shallows. Preparation and defense shape life in Sen'jin Village. Quilboar raids, aggressive sea beasts, and Zalazane's hexes from across the sea threaten the villagers. Herbal remedies and potent alchemical spirits help sustain them.

Vol'jin coordinates the tribe's wider defense from the Horde capital. Meanwhile, local shamans, hunters, and scouts gather recruits arriving from the Valley of Trials. The Darkspear seek resources, guard Durotar's southern flank, and plan Zalazane's downfall.

subzone:shadowglen.text: Shadowglen. Shadowglen is where young night elves begin their training, beneath the boughs of Teldrassil. The whole vale gathers around Aldrassil, a great hollow tree. Inside it, elders, priestesses and mentors guide the young. Only then do they travel farther into the world. Aldrassil is a vast barrow-tree, and it rises in a vale of eternal dusk. The glen lies under the northeastern boughs of the World Tree, and high ridges ring it round. A single narrow pass leads south, toward Starbreeze Village and Dolanaar. With only one way out, the glen stays sheltered and at peace. Yet danger reaches even here. In the far northwest lies Shadowthread Cave, and its venomous spiders threaten the glade. So the young defenders drive them back, along with the vermin and the wild beasts. Then they venture on, deeper among Teldrassil's boughs.

subzone:valley-of-trials.text: Valley of Trials. The Valley of Trials, in the south of Durotar, is where young orcs and Darkspear trolls are put to the test. Chieftains and trainers watch over them from The Den, a shelter cut into the cliffs. Out in the sunlit gulch, the recruits hunt scorpids and cull the angry boars. They keep the lazy peons in line as well, while they gather the valley's scarce timber. The trial is hard. Only those who prove their mettle earn the right to leave as soldiers of the Horde, ready to defend their people. Those who fail are left beneath the desert sun.

topic:alliance-of-lordaeron.text:
Alliance of Lordaeron. Across the Eastern Kingdoms, the Alliance of Lordaeron once held the Old Horde at bay. Seven human kingdoms joined with Khaz Modan dwarves, Wildhammer gryphon riders, gnomes, and high elves in the Second War, under Supreme Commander Anduin Lothar and King Terenas Menethil II. Political fractures and the Scourge broke the coalition during the Third War, yet its legacy endures in today’s Alliance. After Stormwind fell in the First War, Regent Lord Anduin Lothar led its battered refugees across the Great Sea to Capital City. There he pleaded their cause before King Terenas Menethil II. The king called the human rulers to council, though old rivalries and border tensions divided them. The Horde’s threat outweighed those disputes. The seven human nations chose Lothar as Supreme Commander and bound themselves in a desperate pact. The Alliance faced brutal orcish warriors, dark warlocks, and monstrous red dragons. Archbishop Alonsus Faol and Lothar formed the Knights of the Silver Hand, raising holy paladins such as Uther the Lightbringer to counter the Horde’s dark magic. Fighting spread across the Hinterlands, and the siege of Aerie Peak was broken. Then Kurdran Wildhammer pledged his gryphon riders to the skies.

Soon after, the Bronzebeard dwarves and Gnomeregan gnomes were freed. They joined the high elven rangers under Alleria Windrunner. King Perenolde of Alterac betrayed the coalition, but the Alliance drove the Horde back to Blackrock Spire and broke its dominion. Victory left bitterness in place of lasting peace. Disputes flared over the taxes needed to keep the orc internment camps and rebuild Stormwind. Gilneas saw little gain in remaining, built the Greymane Wall, and cut ties. Stromgarde departed over disputes about territory and prisoners, while Quel'Thalas withdrew behind its enchanted runestones. King Terenas tried to hold together the coalition that remained.

During the Third War, the Cult of the Damned and the Plague of Undeath swept across Lordaeron and dismantled it. Arthas Menethil’s betrayal tore out the kingdom’s heart and ended the golden age of the northern realm.

topic:alterac-kingdom.text:
Alterac (kingdom). In the years after the Second War, Alterac lies broken and its capital stands abandoned in the snow. Once one of seven human kingdoms in the Alterac Mountains, it fell when King Aiden Perenolde secretly aided the Old Horde. Now dispossessed nobles and outlaws fight beneath the Syndicate's banner. Alterac began as an Arathorian city-state after the Troll Wars, thousands of years ago. Its settlers held mountain passes and trading outposts. When the empire fractured, they formed an independent realm. Rugged Alterac bordered the prosperous lands of Lordaeron and Stromgarde. Its mountain fighters were tough, yet friction along the border with Thoras Trollbane's Stromgarde left the kingdom isolated long before the Dark Portal opened. Sir Anduin Lothar forged the Alliance of Lordaeron, and King Aiden Perenolde joined with deep reluctance. As Orgrim Doomhammer's Horde swept north, Perenolde believed humanity was doomed. So he secretly made a pact with the Warchief.

In return for Alterac's safety, Perenolde opened fortified mountain passes, plotted against Alliance forces, and sent soldiers and sailors to help the Horde besiege Lordaeron. The betrayal let the orcs reach Capital City far ahead of schedule. When the truth came to light, it shook the Alliance to its core. Stromgarde's forces marched into the mountains, exposed Perenolde's treason, and broke Alterac's military. King Terenas Menethil II placed the fallen nation under martial law. For years, Alliance diplomats argued over who should inherit the throne. After the kingdom collapsed, King Perenolde died in disgrace.

His son, Lord Aliden Perenolde, gathered the bitter, displaced nobles and formed the Syndicate. In orange cloth from their fallen homeland, its bandits and mercenaries now fight ruthlessly to reclaim their ancestral holdings across Hillsbrad and Alterac.

topic:anduin-lothar.text:
Anduin Lothar. In Stormwind's royal court, Anduin Lothar grew up beside Prince Llane Wrynn and Medivh. Last of the ancient Arathi bloodline, he led humanity through the First War and united the northern nations in the Second War as Supreme Commander of the Alliance of Lordaeron. His campaign ended at Blackrock Mountain. Anduin Lothar grew up in Stormwind's royal court, heir to the bloodline of the Arathi kings. He shared his youth with Prince Llane Wrynn and Medivh. Together, the three ventured recklessly into the wilderness and skirmished with Gurubashi trolls in Stranglethorn Vale. Lothar rose through Stormwind's martial ranks and joined the King's Honor Guard. He also earned renown as an Armsman of the Brotherhood of the Horse. On Lordaeron's shores, Lothar brought King Terenas Menethil II grim news of the Horde. His Arathi lineage and standing as a diplomat helped unite the human realms, Ironforge dwarves, and high elves as the Grand Alliance of Lordaeron. Named Supreme Commander, he led the campaign that drove the Horde south to the foot of Blackrock Mountain.

Near the end of the Second War, Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer slew Lothar in a clash there. His death did not break the Alliance. His lieutenant Turalyon took command and led the charge that broke the Horde forever.

topic:argent-dawn.text:
Argent Dawn. Across Azeroth, the Argent Dawn holds its ground against the Scourge and the Burning Legion. Survivors of the Silver Hand formed the order after rejecting the Scarlet Crusade's zealotry. They welcome champions of any race or faction who honor the Light, from Light's Hope Chapel to outposts across Kalimdor. After Highlord Alexandros Mograine fell and Lordaeron collapsed, the Knights of the Silver Hand split over what to do. Grief and paranoia drove many survivors into the xenophobic Scarlet Crusade.

Lord Maxwell Tyrosus and other veterans saw that their former comrades had forsaken the true tenets of the Holy Light. They would neither yield to madness nor abandon the dead kingdom. So they formed the Argent Dawn, ready to defend Azeroth beside any fighter from the Alliance or the Horde. Light's Hope Chapel, in the blighted Eastern Plaguelands, is the Argent Dawn's chief stronghold. From there, the order directs its war against Kel'Thuzad's necromancers and skeletal legions. Its forward camps include Chillwind Camp and a camp outside the Bulwark in Tirisfal Glades.

Argent officers give adventurers enchanted commissions and pay bounties for Scourgestones taken from fallen undead. The Dawn has fewer fighters than the Scarlet Crusade, yet perseverance, unity, and discipline keep it holding the line. Lordaeron remains the Argent Dawn's main battleground, but its watch reaches across Kalimdor and the world's capitals. The order keeps diplomatic presences in Stormwind City, Darnassus, and the goblin trade town of Everlook. In Darkshore and Ashenvale, operatives such as Delgren the Purifier contest demonic cults. Scouts in Desolace and the flooded ruins of Blackfathom Deeps investigate threats involving the Shadow Council and the Twilight's Hammer cult.

topic:arthas-menethil.text: Arthas Menethil. As plague spreads through Lordaeron, Arthas Menethil leaves his place as its golden prince to hunt those behind it. A paladin of the Silver Hand, he claims Frostmourne in the frozen north, loses his soul, kills King Terenas, and turns against his homeland as the Scourge's champion. Arthas grew up heir to King Terenas Menethil II, expected to uphold the ideals of the Alliance of Lordaeron. Muradin Bronzebeard trained him in combat, while Uther the Lightbringer guided him into the Order of the Silver Hand. High and low alike looked to him as humanity's future. Bold, skilled, and fiercely protective of his people, he fought Blackrock clan orc incursions and forest troll warbands. Beneath that bright name lived pride and a deep fear of failure.

topic:black-dragonflight.text: Black dragonflight. From the shadows, the Black dragonflight wages war. The titans charged its dragons to guard Azeroth's deep places, but madness and treachery turned them from that duty. Neltharion became Deathwing, and his surviving brood plots against mortal kingdoms. The titans charged Neltharion and the Black dragonflight with guarding Azeroth's deep caverns and raising its mountains. For ages, they guarded the earth beside the other flights. Their duty brought them near the Old Gods' sunken prisons. Over centuries, dark whispers from those prisons broke Neltharion's mind and turned his brood toward ruin. In the ancient War of the Ancients, Neltharion betrayed the other dragons and became Deathwing the Destroyer. Since then, the Black flight has warred against the red, blue, green, and bronze flights. The other dragons see its cruelty as a profanation of life. Now Black dragons wield magma, black magic, and brimstone to scorch the lands they once tended. Misery and strife spread across mortal realms.

topic:blackrock-clan.text:
Blackrock clan. In Blackrock Mountain, veterans of the Blackrock clan now stand divided between Thrall's New Horde and the Dark Horde. Strict ranks, heavy armor, and skill at the forge once made the clan a force in the First and Second Wars. From Draenor came the Blackrock orcs, whose strength lay in strict ranks, heavy armor, and skill at the forge. Under Chieftain Blackhand, they formed the brutal core of the Old Horde's invasion of Azeroth and laid siege to Stormwind.

Orgrim Doomhammer killed Blackhand to free the Horde from Gul'dan's direct control. Blackrock leaders then commanded both the clan and the Horde through the hard campaigns of the Second War. After the Horde's defeat at Blackrock Mountain, the clan broke apart. Many warriors went to Alliance internment camps, then Thrall freed them and welcomed them into his reformed New Horde.

Others would not yield. They gathered behind Blackhand's sons, Rend and Maim, and withdrew to the heights of Blackrock Spire. There they formed the hostile Dark Horde with remnants of the Dragonmaw and other rogue clans. From his throne in Blackrock Spire, Rend Blackhand claims the title of true Warchief. The Dark Horde keeps a tense truce with the Dark Iron dwarves in the molten depths below, even as it fights both the Alliance and Thrall's Horde.

Clan remnants tainted by demons have also been seen in Lordaeron. There they seek to revive dark sacrificial rites.

topic:bronzebeard-clan.text:
Bronzebeard clan. In Ironforge, King Magni Bronzebeard leads his clan and its kingdom. The Bronzebeards won the War of the Three Hammers, then forged close ties with humanity and the gnomes. Now they anchor the Alliance. High King Modimus Anvilmar’s death opened old rivalries within Ironforge. For years, dwarven society had flourished under his rule, but when he died of old age about two hundred and thirty years ago, those rivalries became civil war. Thane Madoran Bronzebeard commanded Ironforge’s traditional garrison and largest standing army. He drove the Wildhammer and Dark Iron clans from beneath the mountain.

Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan attacked to reclaim Khaz Modan, and Madoran led his clan and army in a decisive campaign. The Bronzebeards shattered the Dark Iron host and secured their supremacy over Ironforge. The Bronzebeards and human kingdoms first met nearly two thousand years ago. Their shared skill in metalcraft, trade, and battle built mutual respect. Then the Orcish Horde swept across the continent in the Second War, and King Magni Bronzebeard brought his realm into the Alliance of Lordaeron.

The Bronzebeards withstood brutal sieges inside their subterranean fortress. Their engineers, gunners, and demolitionists supplied vital firepower and arms, helping turn the tide of war.

topic:burning-blade-clan.text:
Burning Blade clan. Across Durotar and the Barrens, the Burning Blade threatens the young Horde from within. Once renowned for its blademasters, the clan broke under demonic corruption. Now most of its scattered members serve the Shadow Council, while a few honorable blademasters stand with Warchief Thrall. The Burning Blade once fought beside clans such as the Warsong on Draenor. Its blademasters were famed for deadly skill. After drinking Mannoroth’s blood and crossing the Dark Portal into Azeroth during the First War, the clan’s minds broke into chaos.

By the Second War, it had lost all order and raged like a force of nature. These nomadic fighters charged without regard for survival, so ogres held them back until battle called. Near the Dark Portal, the Alliance battered and routed them. Across Kalimdor, Burning Blade covens trouble newly arrived orcs and Darkspear trolls from their first days in the Valley of Trials. Warlocks dwell in Thunder Ridge and keep a major hideout in Skull Rock, near Orgrimmar’s eastern gates. The cultists gather around dark relics such as the Demon Seed and harvest souls for demonic rites. In Durotar and the Barrens, they threaten the young Horde from within.

topic:burning-legion.text:
Burning Legion. Across creation, the Burning Legion remains an infinite host bent on scouring all life. Led by the fallen titan Sargeras, its demons shattered ancient Kalimdor ten thousand years ago, corrupted the orcs, and brought the horrors of the Third War to Azeroth. Sargeras once served the titans, hunting demons across the cosmos and locking them away. Ages of battle convinced him that creation was flawed beyond repair and must burn. He freed the demons he had imprisoned and bent them to his will with fel magic. The corrupted eredar brought intellect to their chaos, and Archimonde and Kil'jaeden became his chief lieutenants. Together they formed an unstoppable engine of cosmic annihilation. Ten thousand years ago, the Highborne's reckless sorceries drew the Burning Legion's gaze to Azeroth. Through the Well of Eternity, Sargeras whispered to Queen Azshara and her councilor Xavius, promising them a chance to reshape the world as a paradise.

The portal unleashed Mannoroth and Archimonde, with swarms of doomguard, felhounds, and flaming infernals. Their war ruined Kalimdor's civilization before night elves, dragonflights, and demigods brought down the gateway. Its catastrophic implosion tore the supercontinent apart in the Great Sundering, scattering ruined lands across vast new seas. The Legion was cast back into the Twisting Nether, yet Azeroth remained in its sights. Kil'jaeden arranged proxy cataclysms from afar. The deceiver bound the orcs of Draenor through demonic blood pacts, and the Horde charged through the Dark Portal to weaken mortal defenses.

When that failed, the Legion forged the Lich King and unleashed the undead Scourge across Lordaeron, paving the way for Archimonde's return in the Third War. Archimonde fell at Mount Hyjal, but Legion remnants still linger across Felwood, the Blasted Lands, and hidden cults throughout the world.

topic:cenarion-circle.text:
Cenarion Circle. Across Azeroth, the Cenarion Circle guards nature’s balance. Founded by Malfurion Stormrage under Cenarius, it keeps its sacred haven in Moonglade and tends the Emerald Dream and blighted lands. Once made up of night elves, it now welcomes tauren druids to defend the living world. Thousands of years ago, Cenarius taught Malfurion Stormrage, the first mortal druid. After the Great Sundering, Malfurion gathered those who wished to learn nature’s ways. The order made its home in Moonglade’s sacred vale. Ever since, the Circle has watched over Azeroth’s wild places. The Cenarion Circle is rooted in night elf history, yet answers neither to Darnassus nor to the Sisterhood of Elune. Its heart is Moonglade, where the peaceful town of Nighthaven keeps an ancient truce. Weapons stay sheathed there, beyond the reach of mortal wars.

After the Third War, Malfurion and Hamuul Runetotem, a tauren elder, became friends and came to respect one another. The Circle honored the tauren’s reverence for the Earth Mother and welcomed Hamuul into its ranks. Through him, druidism returned to his people after thousands of years.

topic:cenarius.text:
Cenarius. Across Kalimdor, Cenarius guards the wild places and teaches the night elves druidism. The ancient demigod, son of Elune and Malorne, guided mortal druids for thousands of years before falling in battle during the Third War. Born to Elune, goddess of the moon, and Malorne, the great white stag demigod, Cenarius was bound to the mortal world and placed in Malorne's care. Ysera the Dreamer took him as a foster son and guided him along the infinite paths of the Emerald Dream. Cenarius held power over living wood and earth. He fathered the Keepers of the Grove and the dryads, binding his bloodline to Kalimdor's wild places. Millennia ago, Malfurion Stormrage, his twin Illidan, and Tyrande Whisperwind sought the legendary demigod. Cenarius saw Malfurion's exceptional heart and trained him as the first mortal druid. When Queen Azshara and her Highborne unleashed the Burning Legion in the War of the Ancients, Cenarius gathered Kalimdor's wild demigods to fight beside the mortal defenders. For ten thousand years after the Great Sundering, Cenarius watched over Kalimdor and nurtured the Cenarion Circle with Malfurion. During the Third War, the Warsong clan began cutting timber in Ashenvale. Angered by the ruin of sacred woodlands, Cenarius drove the invaders back.

Then Grom Hellscream and his warriors took Mannoroth's demonic blood. Filled with demonic fury, the corrupted orcs overwhelmed Cenarius and struck him down. Nature's defenders were left in deep sorrow.

topic:church-of-the-holy-light.text:
Church of the Holy Light. After Lordaeron's fall, the Church of the Holy Light gathers in Stormwind City's Cathedral of Light. Its clergy guide human souls through compassion, justice, and devotion. Among the humans of Arathor, faith in the Holy Light took root more than a thousand years ago. The faithful learned to channel it to heal injuries and purge affliction. They were taught to give charity and seek righteousness, believing the Light dwells within all thinking beings. In time, these beliefs became an organized faith. Lordaeron became its heartland, with revered sanctuaries in Stratholme, Andorhal, Tyr's Hand, and Light's Hope Chapel. In the First War, the Brotherhood of Northshire went to battle, healing defenders who fell against the invading Orcish Horde. The clerics had no weapons or heavy armor, and suffered terrible losses to the orcs. During the Second War, Archbishop Alonsus Faol met with Supreme Commander Anduin Lothar.

Together they formed the Knights of the Silver Hand, holy warriors who could wield holy wrath and endure physical combat. Paladins and priests became the Alliance of Lordaeron's moral and martial bulwark, preserving humanity from annihilation. The Third War brought sorrow to the faithful. As the Plague of Undeath spread across Lordaeron, the Church aided the sick and tried to contain the contamination. But the kingdom collapsed from within, and the clergy could not stem the disaster.

Lordaeron is now a wilderness haunted by the Scourge, so the Church moved its seat south. Under Archbishop Benedictus, its clergy rebuilt their hierarchy in Stormwind's newly constructed Cathedral of Light. There they offer solace, spiritual guidance, and military purpose to the battered survivors of the Alliance.

topic:cult-of-the-damned.text:
Cult of the Damned. Across Lordaeron, the Cult of the Damned still serves the Lich King. Before the Third War, its poisoned grain spread the Scourge and helped bring down humanity's greatest kingdom. Now cultists tend plague cauldrons and necromantic academies in the Plaguelands, while living agents infiltrate the cities of the living. Kel'Thuzad founded the cult after hearing the Lich King's whispers from the Frozen Throne. Exiled from the Kirin Tor, the archmage returned to Lordaeron with great wealth and forbidden arts. To the desperate poor, he promised equality and freedom from misery. To wealthy landowners such as House of Barov, he promised eternal life and lasting power over their domains. Both were drawn into a death cult meant to betray their homeland from within. Beneath Caer Darrow, cultists practiced necromancy in secret. They built abominations and perfected the Plague of Undeath brought from Northrend. Then they contaminated grain stores in Andorhal, Lordaeron's breadbasket.

Flour traveled along merchant routes to homes across the Eastweald. Within days, commoners sickened and died, then rose as thralls under the Lich King's command. When Prince Arthas killed Kel'Thuzad in Andorhal, the cult had already spread too far to stop the kingdom's fall. The Cult of the Damned still threatens northern Lordaeron under the resurrected archlich Kel'Thuzad. Living cultists operate from the ruins of Stratholme and Scholomance. They perform dark rites, tend plague cauldrons among ruined farms, and try to kill Scarlet Crusaders and Forsaken. Their agents pass unnoticed through settlements, poison wells, disrupt supplies, and recruit others for the Scourge.

topic:dark-iron-clan.text:
Dark Iron clan. In Blackrock Mountain, the Dark Iron clan serves Ragnaros under Emperor Dagran Thaurissan. Driven from Ironforge in the War of the Three Hammers, they called the Firelord from beneath the earth and fell beneath his rule. The War of the Three Hammers began when High King Modimus Anvilmar died. Three dwarven factions had shared Ironforge, but the Bronzebeards defeated both rivals in the civil war. They drove out the Wildhammers and Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan's Dark Irons.

Thaurissan swore vengeance and founded a settlement in the Redridge Mountains. His sorceress wife, Modgud, led an army against Grim Batol. Both assaults failed, and the united Bronzebeard and Wildhammer armies marched on Thaurissan's stronghold. Desperate, he tried to free an apocalyptic being beneath the earth. His ritual broke through the world's core and released Ragnaros the Firelord. Ragnaros's return shattered the peaks around him and formed Blackrock Mountain's blazing caldera. The Searing Gorge and the Burning Steppes lie beside it. The cataclysm killed Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan, and the surviving Dark Irons became the Firelord's servants.

Over the centuries, they built Shadowforge City in the mountain's lower chambers. Their artisans and sorcerers mastered stone golems, dark sorceries, and steam-driven siege engines. Under the watch of flamewakers and elemental overlords, they made weapons from the molten elements around them.

topic:dark-iron-dwarf.text:
Dark Iron dwarf. Beneath Blackrock Mountain, Dark Iron dwarves live under Ragnaros's rule. Banished from Ironforge after the War of the Three Hammers, they have built a society shaped by fire and tyranny. Dark Iron dwarves have dark gray or soot-black skin and eyes like glowing embers. Their Bronzebeard and Wildhammer cousins look different. Their people split during the War of the Three Hammers, when Sorcerer-thane Thaurissan tried to conquer Ironforge. Defeated, he led them south into the Redridge Mountains.

There, he sought dark powers to avenge his losses and released Ragnaros the Firelord from the Elemental Plane. The summoning shattered the surrounding peaks into the volcanic waste of Blackrock Mountain. It bound the Dark Iron to fiery servitude. Life in Shadowforge, deep beneath the mountain, is brutal. The Dark Irons were once ambitious and cunning, but generations beneath Ragnaros's oppressive aura have warped much of their culture. Cruelty, paranoia, and tyranny now shape it.

Dark Iron law gives one sentence for infractions: trial by combat in the Ring of the Law. Poisoning and political intrigue run so deep that Dark Iron travelers bring their own rations rather than trust food from strangers. Not all Dark Iron dwarves serve Emperor Dagran Thaurissan and the cult of Ragnaros. Dissident factions have broken away to follow their own ends. The best known is the Thorium Brotherhood, a guild of master smiths based at Thorium Point in Searing Gorge. They left the main clan and hire outsiders to fight their former masters.

Other Dark Irons work as mercenaries, spies, or trade engineers alongside neutral groups such as the Venture Company.

topic:dark-riders.text: Dark Riders. In Duskwood, the Dark Riders hunt magical relics and terrorize the land. Hooded and merciless, they strike from hiding and leave slaughter behind. Little is known of the Dark Riders' beginnings. Witnesses speak of hooded horsemen with harsh, shrill voices. One was seen using a small gem to receive orders from a master it called only its “Lord.” Across the kingdom, they hunt objects of magical power. Anyone who stands between them and their prize is cut down.

topic:darkspear-tribe.text:
Darkspear tribe. Across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms, the Darkspear tribe follows Thrall’s Horde. Driven from Stranglethorn Vale and rescued from a sea witch in the Great Sea, the jungle trolls follow Shadow Hunter Vol’jin from Sen’jin Village. They now struggle to reclaim the Echo Isles from Zalazane. Once part of the broken Gurubashi Empire in Stranglethorn Vale, the Darkspear were smaller and less ruthless than their neighbors. For centuries, they endured famine and fought the brutal Bloodscalp and Skullsplitter tribes. Driven out to sea, they settled on remote islands, where murlocs, Kul Tiran sailors, and a naga sea witch threatened them.

Their elder chieftain, Sen’jin, was captured and slain in dark rites beneath the sea. Before he died, he foretold that the orc Warchief Thrall would lead the Darkspear to a new destiny. Thrall’s fleet rescued the survivors. They pledged loyalty to the new Horde and sailed west to Kalimdor. The Darkspear have adapted quickly to the Horde’s values of honor, unlike their cannibalistic jungle kin. They have enclaves in Malaka’jin in the Stonetalon Mountains, Shadowprey Village in Desolace, and Zoram’gar Outpost in Ashenvale. In Orgrimmar, they make their spiritual home in the Valley of Spirits, where shadow hunters and witch doctors commune with the loa.

Their scouts, bat riders, and powerful hexes are respected. Yet old traditions run deep, and some ancient rites their allies frown upon are still practiced quietly in the dark.

topic:dragonmaw-clan.text:
Dragonmaw clan. Across Khaz Modan, Dragonmaw remnants still lurk in wetlands and mountains. During the Second War, they became infamous for subduing and riding red dragons. After Alexstrasza was freed, the scattered orcs remained hostile to both the Alliance and Thrall's New Horde. The Dragonmaw crossed the Dark Portal from Draenor with the Old Horde. On Azeroth, they turned their skill toward subduing its winged terrors. Black dragon Deathwing whispered to Zuluhed the Whacked, chieftain of the Dragonmaw, and led him to an ancient golden disk called the Dragon Soul. Zuluhed gave it to Nekros Skullcrusher, his greatest warlock. Nekros drew on its fel taint and named it the Demon Soul. With its agonizing power, he ensnared Alexstrasza the Life-Binder.

The Dragonmaw fortified Grim Batol, an abandoned dwarven bastion, and chained the Dragonqueen in darkness. During the Second War, they forced her red dragon brood to serve the Old Horde as aerial dreadnoughts. The Dragonmaw reign ended when the Demon Soul was destroyed, freeing Alexstrasza and her flight from psychic torment. Alexstrasza devoured Nekros Skullcrusher, and her vengeful flight laid waste to Grim Batol. The clan's strength broke.

Routed and terrified, survivors scattered into the Wetlands' marshy bogs and the jagged peaks around Grim Batol. The Dragonmaw who remain on Azeroth are desperate, feral renegades. They fiercely guard their dwindling camps against dwarven patrols and vengeful dragons, and remain hostile to both the Alliance and Thrall's New Horde.

topic:elune.text:
Elune. Across Azeroth, Elune is chiefly worshipped by the night elves as their protector and mother of Cenarius. The larger moon, the White Lady, is hers, and her gifts reach from healing and peace to lunar fury. Tauren know her as Mu'sha, the gentle left eye of the Earth Mother. Elune is one of the few true deities known across Azeroth, bound to the night sky and the larger moon, the White Lady. Though she has never appeared in bodily form, night elven artists portray her as a radiant kaldorei with alabaster skin, silver hair, and eyes of pure moonlight. Ancient kaldorei legends say she rested in the depths of the Well of Eternity by day, whispering wisdom to the first night elves. Night elven life, both sacred and civic, centers on devotion to Elune through the Sisterhood of Elune. High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind leads this ancient order. The Sisters call on Elune to mend even lethal wounds, and turn her radiant wrath upon their foes with searing starlight.

Elune and the Great White Stag, Malorne, brought forth Cenarius. Through him, Elune's heavenly mysteries are bound to the druidic traditions that tend Kalimdor's wildlands. Elune is known for peace, harmony, and restoration, yet battle has its place in her worship. As the Night Warrior, she is a fierce patron of battle. She gathers the spirits of fallen heroes and sets them in the heavens, where they ride as stars.

The nomadic tauren call Elune Mu'sha, the radiant left eye of the Earth Mother. She lights the night and guides wandering hunters beside her fiery twin, An'she the sun.

topic:emerald-dream.text: Emerald Dream. Druids and green dragons keep watch over the Emerald Dream, where Azeroth’s wild nature runs free. Its lands shift with ancient rhythms, and druids enter to seek communion with the cycle of life. The Emerald Dream shows Azeroth as it might have been without intelligent beings clearing forests or raising cities. Though it lies beyond the physical world, it remains bound to Azeroth’s heartbeat. Shaped during the ancient ordering of the world, it holds forests, plains, and rivers in a wilderness that never rests in one form. Time and distance lose their usual meaning there. A day in the waking world can feel like decades, while landmarks shift before mortal eyes. After the ordering of the world, the titans entrusted the Emerald Dream to Ysera the Dreamer, great Aspect of the green dragonflight. She guides Azeroth’s natural rhythms and evolution, dwelling in an unending trance. Through enchanted dreamsight, she perceives both the waking world and its spirit reflection. Green dragons guard the rare natural portals between the physical world and the Dream, watching the boundary between sleep and waking. For mortal druids, the Emerald Dream is the wellspring of their craft. Through nature magic, they send their spirits into the Dream while their bodies rest in barrow dens, sometimes for years or centuries. There they commune with ancient nature spirits and the Wild Gods, seeking insight into the Great Cycle of life and death. Skilled dreamwalkers move beyond physical laws in their dreamforms. They can cross vast distances or pass through solid barriers.

topic:explorers-league.text:
Explorers' League. Across Azeroth, the Explorers' League seeks the lost beginnings of the dwarves.
