Twilight's Hammer. Across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms, Twilight's Hammer works in secret to bring Azeroth to its end. Its creed calls for the Old Gods to awaken and all things to end. On Draenor, Twilight's Hammer began as an orc clan of the Old Horde. Two-headed ogre-mage Cho'gall led the clan and served as one of Gul'dan's chief lieutenants in the Shadow Council. Under Cho'gall, its members embraced a grim creed that looked toward the end of all things. They came to see the Horde as a force of destruction for that purpose. Twilight's Hammer crossed the Dark Portal during the First War, and its apocalyptic zeal deepened on Azeroth. Its cultists heard the true whispers of the Old Gods, ancient horrors chained beneath the earth. Blackhand tolerated their erratic rituals because Cho'gall kept their bloodlust in check. He sent them with Kilrogg Deadeye's Bleeding Hollow clan in early assaults on Stormwind Keep.

During the Second War, the clan worked deep inside Grim Batol, overseeing critical refineries until Gul'dan's betrayal fractured the Horde. Orgrim Doomhammer ordered the traitorous clan slaughtered near the Tomb of Sargeras. A core of zealots survived. On Kalimdor's forgotten shores, Twilight's Hammer grew from a broken orc clan into a secret, multiracial conspiracy. It draws disillusioned members from both the Alliance and the Horde, recruiting any soul broken enough to welcome oblivion. In northern Kalimdor, Twilight Lord Kelris leads cultists entrenched in the submerged halls of Blackfathom Deeps. There they feed sacrifices to Aku'mai, a monstrous servant of an Old God.

Farther north in Darkshore, their excavators disturb the colossal fossilized remains at the Master's Glaive. In Silithus's southern deserts, robed fanatics tend abyssal windstones and listen for ancient horrors stirring beneath the sands.

topic:venture-company.text: Venture Company. Across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms, Venture Company crews strip-mine and clear-cut land, heedless of its people and nature. Mogul Razdunk directs the ruthless goblin cartel from afar. Its crews seek raw materials with heavy machinery, away from major goblin ports like Booty Bay and Ratchet. Venture Company crews tear into the land for raw materials. Mogul Razdunk directs the cartel from afar, and workers wield heavy machinery across Azeroth. Shredders harvest timber, drilling rigs bore into the earth, and refineries process what they find. The cartel takes resources by force, ignoring treaties, borders, and local rights.

topic:westfall-brigade.text: People's Militia. In Westfall, the People's Militia holds its ground against the Defias Brotherhood. Gryan Stoutmantle raised the volunteers at Sentinel Hill after Stormwind withdrew its troops. With local farmers and visiting adventurers, they defend the region from banditry. Westfall once fed the Kingdom of Stormwind. Then the kingdom withdrew its troops, leaving the people defenseless. The Defias Brotherhood spread across the plains, seizing family homesteads, taking over iron mines, and extorting local farmers. With no royal reinforcements in sight, veteran warrior Gryan Stoutmantle rallied citizens and retired soldiers to form the People's Militia. Sentinel Tower, atop Sentinel Hill, is the Militia's base. From there, volunteers patrol the region's main roads with little military gear or steady supplies. Gryan Stoutmantle directs them against the growing ranks of Defias highwaymen, thieves, and pillagers. When Redridge asks for mutual aid, the Militia must refuse. Sending even a handful of men could leave Westfall lost.

topic:worgen.text:
Worgen. Across Silverpine Forest, Ashenvale, and Duskwood, Worgen now hunt with bestial swiftness and a fury they cannot master. Once feared as nightmares from another realm, their beginnings remain uncertain. Long before Worgen appeared in Lordaeron and Kalimdor, people told folktales and cautionary tales of wolf-men. Their beginnings remain a mystery. Scholars who have studied them believe they came to Azeroth from another realm. Archmage Arugal and the night elves' Scythe of Elune have both been shown to summon them. During the Third War, the Scourge overran Lordaeron, and slain Kirin Tor wizards rose again as undead. Archmage Arugal sought a weapon to strengthen Dalaran's dwindling ranks. He used forbidden research by the Dalaran wizard Ur to pierce the veil and summon Worgen into Silverpine Forest. They savaged the undead invaders, but Arugal could not master their fury. The beasts turned on the wizards and spread their curse with fang and claw.

Mad with guilt and fascination, Arugal claimed the monsters as his children. He seized Baron Silverlaine's ancestral seat and renamed it Shadowfang Keep. There, he cursed nearby villagers into monstrous nocturnal servitude.

zone:alterac.text:
Alterac Mountains. Across the Alterac Mountains, ruined peaks shelter ogres, outlaws, and the remnants of arcane power. Once home to the human kingdom of Alterac and Dalaran’s scholarly magocracy, these highlands draw travelers from nearby foothill settlements and the rebuilding city. During the Second War, Alterac stood among humanity’s Seven Kingdoms. King Aiden Perenolde betrayed the Alliance of Lordaeron and joined the Old Horde, hoping to save his realm. His treachery was uncovered and crushed, and the kingdom broke into disputed borderlands. After Alterac dissolved, the Third War brought fresh horrors. Its grand stone capital now lies in ruins.

The Crushridge ogres occupy the Ruins of Alterac under Mug'thol’s leadership. Alterac’s surviving human nobles formed the Syndicate, a vicious band of criminals. They fight by force to reclaim their lost estates. On the mountains’ western edge, Dalaran’s surviving magi rebuild beside lordamere lake. The demon lord Archimonde devastated the great city-state during the Third War. Its magi raised a massive, opaque violet dome over the ruins, but the shield has since been removed. The kirin tor now rebuild their sanctum in the open. Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver can be found inside the Violet Citadel. Southshore and Tarren Mill are staging grounds for journeys into the peaks. Yeti, mountain lions, and Syndicate footpads roam here. Beneath the snow line, a greater conflict churns.

Deep in the mountain passes, the dwarven Stormpike Guard and the reclusive Frostwolf clan of orcs contest Alterac Valley. They fight over ancient territorial and mining rights.

zone:arathi.text:
Arathi Highlands. In Arathi, ruined Stromgarde leaves the highlands at war on several fronts. The kingdom's remnants, the Horde, Syndicate nobles, and invading ogres fight for the ancient birthplace of the Empire of Arathor in southeastern Lordaeron. The dry plains of Arathi once formed the heart of a united human realm. Millennia ago, King Thoradin gathered the divided tribes beneath the Arathi banner and built their capital, Strom, on ground that was easy to defend. During the Troll Wars, humanity made its compact with the high elves here and learned the arcane arts to drive back the Amani.

Noble bloodlines later spread north into Lordaeron and south toward Stormwind. The imperial guard remained and formed Stromgarde, a martial kingdom that guarded the border against forest trolls for ages. Under King Thoras Trollbane, Stromgarde helped defend the Alliance during the Second War. The Third War and its aftermath broke the kingdom. It escaped the worst of the Scourge plague, but King Thoras's mysterious death plunged the realm into turmoil. Boulderfist ogres came down from the hills, while nobles of Alterac in the Syndicate seized wide districts of Stromgarde Keep.

Prince Galen Trollbane and his loyalists now hold a small part of the city and their refuge at Refuge Pointe. Against heavy odds, they fight a bitter guerrilla war.

zone:ashenvale.text:
Ashenvale. Ashenvale's sacred woods have become a battleground as the Horde cuts timber for Orgrimmar. Between the Barrens and Darkshore, the ancient forest remains under the care of the Sentinels and Cenarius. Its canopy shelters moonwells and old ruins, while demonic blights, hostile tribes, and a contested frontier threaten the woods. Beneath Mount Hyjal, Ashenvale has belonged to the kaldorei and the children of Cenarius for millennia. Immense trees knit a close canopy overhead. Daily rain gathers as mist beneath them, and twilight settles on the forest floor.

Moss covers the ruins of elven settlements, where walking ancients and dryads keep watch. For thousands of years, the night elves built no true cities here. They hunted lightly and kept the wild domain in balance. The Third War shattered Ashenvale's peace. Grommash Hellscream and the Warsong clan entered the forest for lumber, and their demonic bloodlust led them to slay Cenarius. Now the struggle is a full territorial war.

From Splintertree Post and the southern Mor'shan Rampart, the Warsong Outriders send axes and shredders into the eastern woods to supply Orgrimmar. The Silverwing Sentinels hold Astranaar, a sanctuary town. They have sworn to drive every orcish logger from the sacred grove. The lumber war is only one danger in Ashenvale. The Burning Legion left blighted scars at Felfire Hill and Demon Fall Canyon, where Mannoroth died. Satyrs make their bases in ruins such as Satyrnaar and Xavian, corrupting waterways and wildlife.

Furbolg tribes, once friends of the elves, have largely fallen to dark madness. Mysterious worgen stalk the northern shrine near Felwood. Cursed dragonkin prowl Bough Shadow and guard a portal into the troubled Emerald Dream.

zone:azshara.text: Azshara. Along northeastern Kalimdor, Azshara’s broken coast runs from autumn woods to drowned ruins and perilous waters. Horde and Alliance outposts stand near its borders, while naga, ghosts, and other dangers haunt the land. Zin-Azshari’s coast once lay at the heart of kaldorei civilization. Ten thousand years ago, Queen Azshara and her Highborne court drew the Burning Legion into Azeroth. So began the War of the Ancients. The Well of Eternity collapsed and the sea swallowed most of the magnificent city. Fractured cliffs, perilous coral reefs, and waterlogged spires remain. Survivors named the ruined land for their fallen monarch, whose pride and betrayal changed it forever. Crimson, orange, and gold leaves cover Azshara’s woods through an autumn that never ends. Yet the quiet canopy hides a harsh wilderness. Satyrs perform dark rituals in forest hollows, Highborne apparitions haunt drowned foundations, and Spitelash naga prowl the Coral Sea’s shallow reefs. Ferocious beasts, giant hydras, and mountain giants roam the highlands and ivory beaches. Azshara’s isolation and harsh terrain draw those who pursue forgotten crafts or watch dangerous powers. Archmage Xylem lives in a secluded tower high above the cliffs. There, he tests promising spellcasters and cunning rogues. Farther along the coast, the demon hunter Loramus Thalipedes watches the waves from a barren isle. At a temple above the churning waters, the immense sea giant Lord Arkkoroc demands blood sacrifices.

zone:badlands.text: Badlands. Dust storms sweep across the Badlands, where rival forces hold ground in dwarven Khaz Modan. Dark Iron dwarves, troggs, Dustbelcher ogres, and black dragonkin crowd this frontier between Loch Modan and Searing Gorge. Uldaman's titan ruins and the Horde stronghold of Kargath make it a crossroads. South of Loch Modan's green hills, you enter a hot basin of barren flats and rugged ravines. Coyotes, cougars, and vultures roam the land, and fierce sandstorms can hide the horizon. Dustbelcher ogres keep crude camps across the plateaus. At Angor Fortress, the Dark Iron clan fortifies its hold and clashes with anyone who trespasses. Among the northern bluffs lies Uldaman, an underground complex carved by the titan-forged earthen. Ironforge prospectors recently uncovered it, revealing monumental secrets about the ancient ancestry of the dwarven race. Their digging awoke hordes of vicious Stonevault troggs and animated earthen guardians. The creatures slaughtered the archaeological teams and turned the digsites outside into bloody skirmish grounds. The Horde holds one of its most precarious footholds in the southern Eastern Kingdoms here. Kargath, in the northwest, gives Warchief Thrall's forces a base to watch the rogue Dark Horde in nearby Blackrock Mountain. Far to the east, Lethlor Ravine cuts a treacherous chasm through the land. Beneath the mountains' shadow, black whelps and dangerous black dragonkin guard their brooding grounds.

zone:barrens.text:
The Barrens. Across The Barrens, Horde outposts guard the roads as rival forces press in from every side. Once forest before the Great Sundering, this central Kalimdor plain is now dry country of red dust, scrub, and wandering wildlife. The Crossroads anchors Horde traffic, but quilboar, centaur, and creeping corruption threaten its hold. For generations, tauren nomads hunted kodo and zhevra across these plains. They also fought a recurring defensive war against the Kolkar centaur. During the Third War, Thrall led the orcs to Kalimdor. He helped Cairne Bloodhoof drive back the centaur, then crossed the savanna into Mulgore with him. The Barrens now links Durotar, Mulgore, and Ashenvale.

The Crossroads and Camp Taurajo guard trade along the Gold Road. Orcish homesteads endure the harsh climate as the Horde builds a lasting home. Horde control of the savanna remains contested. Razormane quilboar raid farms and supply lines from thorn-choked strongholds, their bristles like porcupine quills. To the south, the dens of Razorfen Kraul loom over the land. On the eastern coast, Theramore forces hold Northwatch Hold, while dwarven prospectors dig into the titan complex of Bael Modan. Ratchet's goblins keep uneasy neutrality in trade and welcome travelers who bring coin.

zone:blackfathom.text:
Blackfathom Deeps. In the flooded halls of Blackfathom Deeps, Twilight's Hammer cultists gather along Ashenvale's northwestern shore. The temple once honored Elune, the night elven moon goddess. Naga and satyrs now venerate Aku'mai, a primordial hydra and servant of an Old God. Blackfathom Deeps lies sunken beneath the coastal waters of the Veiled Sea. Before the Great Sundering, Highborne masons raised gem-encrusted bridges through its halls, and Queen Azshara guarded the waters around its sacred moonwell. She kept salt seas and mountain streams apart. When the Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor ten thousand years ago, the temple sank. It lay undisturbed for millennia, until foul whispers rose from the darkness below. Twilight's Hammer cultists came to the sunken ruins, drawn by mad dreams and dark portents. Inside, they forged an unholy truce with coastal naga led by Lady Sarevess and prowling satyrs. Together, they desecrated the moonwell and enslaved nearby creatures.

Years of torment drove the giant sea turtle Ghamoo-ra mad. The brutal murloc Gelihast raised a blood shrine, and the caverns filled with fresh sacrifices. Under Twilight Lord Kelris, the cultists made the ruins a staging ground for the Old Gods' impending return.

zone:blastedlands.text:
Blasted Lands. In the Blasted Lands, Nethergarde Keep watches a wasteland scarred by the Dark Portal. Red clay and barren rock cover the former Black Morass, while demons and Dreadmaul ogres still threaten the region. Once, the Blasted Lands belonged to the Black Morass, a stretch of dense fenland. During the First War, the warlock Gul'dan and the possessed Medivh tore open the Dark Portal and unleashed the orcish Horde. Fel energies poured through the breach. They drained the land of moisture and baked it into cracked red clay.

The Portal was destroyed at the end of the Second War. Its shockwaves scorched the ground again and turned the native stone crimson. Nethergarde Keep watches the only road into the valley from the northern bluffs. Archmage Khadgar and the Kirin Tor commissioned the stone fortress after the Second War. Its mages and soldiers are sworn to stop renewed demonic or orcish incursions.

The posting is strict. Garrison members who break its rules are banished to the Stockade in Stormwind. Dreadmaul ogres remained after Draenor's fall and keep the defenders under pressure. They raid the roads and attack the gates under fell guidance. The Tainted Scar cuts through the southwestern Blasted Lands, a cratered canyon filled with demons. After the Legion's defeat at Mount Hyjal, doomguard commander Lord Kazzak gathered wandering demons, doomguard, and felhounds under his banner. His dreadlord lieutenant, Razelikh the Defiler, directs the Shadowsworn cultists at the Altar of Storms and commands the local Dreadmaul ogres. Scholars and wanderers still brave the Blasted Lands in search of discoveries. Just inside the northern pass, Bloodmage Drazial and Bloodmage Lynnore experiment with organs from scorpids, basilisks, and boars. They use them to brew potent physical enhancers.

Farther into the wastes, the draenei hermit Kum'isha seeks scattered draenethyst fragments, remnants of Draenor's shattered past. Travelers who recover them receive a reward from him.

zone:burningsteppes.text:
Burning Steppes. At Blackrock Mountain’s southern base, fire and lava have scorched the Burning Steppes. The land holds the main overland passage between Stormwind and Khaz Modan, where hostile clans and dragons threaten travelers. The Burning Steppes were once the northern reaches of the Redridge Mountains. Centuries ago, during the War of the Three Hammers, the exiled Dark Iron clan built Thaurissan as its capital here. Facing defeat by the Bronzebeard and Wildhammer clans, Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan tried to summon elemental forces.

His spell shattered the surrounding mountains and brought Ragnaros the Firelord into Azeroth. Rivers of lava opened, and Blackrock Mountain rose from the earth. The blast left the steppes charred and barren. During the Second War, Blackrock Spire became the Old Horde’s foremost seat of power. Near the war’s end, the Grand Alliance of Lordaeron marched into the Burning Steppes and laid siege to the mountain. At its foot, Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer struck down Lord Anduin Lothar.

Lothar’s death spurred the Allied armies to rout the orcs and win the war. Ash and rusted steel still mark the valley where the battle was fought. Blackrock orcs remain in the steppes, keeping the Old Horde’s cruelty despite Thrall’s New Horde in distant Kalimdor. From Blackrock Stronghold, they ally with the black dragonflight and Firegut ogres. They honor no truce.

Dark Iron dwarves and elemental servitors haunt the fiery ruins. Black drakes and wyrmkin prey on travelers crossing between Stormwind and the northern kingdoms.

zone:darkshore.text:
Darkshore. Auberdine links Darkshore to night elf lands and the wider Alliance. Travelers reach this cold, misty coast in northwestern Kalimdor from Teldrassil or the Eastern Kingdoms. Ancient ruins and troubled wildlife mark the land, while cultists, naga, and a creeping rot threaten it. Darkshore lies beneath the western shadows of Mount Hyjal and Felwood. Pine groves give way to fog and cold, rocky shores. Millennia ago, the Kaldorei cities of Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran flourished here. The Great Sundering shattered them, leaving pillars and arches half-drowned or tangled in roots. Highborne spirits haunt the ruins, while scavenging murlocs and invading naga roam among them. After the Third War and the planting of Teldrassil, the night elves made Auberdine a busy haven on this wild coast. Ships arrive from Rut'theran Village, Stormwind Harbor, and Menethil Harbor in the distant Wetlands by way of Southshore. Auberdine links night elf lands to the rest of the Alliance. Sentinels patrol the trade road south to Ashenvale, but their small garrison cannot watch the deep wilds beyond it. A slow, malignant rot has reached Darkshore beneath the eastern mountains. Corrupted runoff from Felwood flows to sources such as Cliffspring Falls, poisoning the water and driving bears, stags, and the furbolgs of Blackwood Den into violent madness.

The Dark Strand cultists perform foul rites at the Tower of Althalaxx. Twilight's Hammer gathers around the ancient and terrifying monument called the Master's Glaive.

zone:darnassus.text: Darnassus. High among the branches of Teldrassil lies Darnassus, the city of the night elves. Tyrande Whisperwind and the druids guide it. Its people are ancient, but they are mortal now. They must learn to live without their undying life, and they seek new ties with the Alliance. Darnassus spreads across the upper canopy of the World Tree, off the coast of northern Kalimdor. Its wooden halls and winding paths circle a quiet lake. Bridges join the terraces of tradesmen and craftsmen, of Sentinels and druids. The wild is never far from the city's daily life. Beside the long history of the kaldorei, Darnassus is young. In the Third War, Nordrassil was sacrificed, and the night elves came to know age and sickness. So Archdruid Fandral Staghelm and his followers planted Teldrassil, hoping to restore their lost vitality. The city grew up among its boughs, a refuge and a monument to their survival. Yet already a malaise stirs among the roots. Two powers hold sway in Darnassus. From the Temple of the Moon, High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind commands the Sentinels and guides her people's faith. Across the waterways, Fandral leads the druids, for Malfurion Stormrage is lost in the Emerald Dream. To their new Alliance partners, the two leaders show a united face. But between priestesses and druids, the friction lingers.

zone:deadmines.text:
The Deadmines. Beneath Moonbrook, the Deadmines hide the Defias Brotherhood's staging ground. Once a source of the kingdom’s gold, the tunnels were abandoned in the First War and long feared as haunted. Edwin VanCleef and goblin engineers now work there beyond the realm’s eyes, building an engine of vengeance against Stormwind. Before the First War, the Deadmines were called the greatest gold-producing center in human lands. Their gold supplied a third of Stormwind’s reserves. When the Orcish Horde swept through the kingdom and razed the capital, the mines were hastily abandoned to darkness.

Sir Anduin Lothar spent twenty months imprisoned by subterranean ogres while recovering the sacred Tome of Divinity. Warchief Blackhand’s rebellious daughter Griselda fled into the lower passages with the ogre Turok, and both met their ends there. Believed cursed and home only to shambling undead and lurking subterranean vermin, the depths lay untouched for decades. After the Stonemasons’ Guild was cast out of Stormwind without payment for rebuilding the city, Edwin VanCleef gathered the disgruntled artisans into the Defias Brotherhood. Seeking a secure headquarters beyond the reach of Gryan Stoutmantle’s People’s Militia, the Brotherhood chose its central redoubt in the abandoned tunnels.

They drove out the legitimate Miners’ League, leaving Foreman Thistlenettle’s doomed workers to perish and rise as undead ghouls. Lumbering ogres, seasoned brigands, and mechanical constructs guard the shafts, now an industrial war camp. Picks, fires, and illicit industry echo through the lower mines once more.

zone:deadwind.text:
Deadwind Pass. A foul wind sweeps Deadwind Pass, where the road runs between Duskwood and the Swamp of Sorrows. Karazhan rises at the heart of the pass, its ruined tower still tainted by Medivh's death. Ogres and ghosts haunt the canyon, and no town offers shelter. Deadwind Pass lies between Duskwood and the Swamp of Sorrows. Its ravines cut through pale stone and petrified wood. Once counted as part of the Redridge Mountains, the pass is now a hollow scar. A foul wind tears through the gorge, and sudden lightning under a gray sky makes metal arms dangerous to carry.

Totemic effigies hang from dead branches beside the main road, warning travelers to keep moving. No fertile soil or mineable veins offer reason to stay. No town or flight master can give aid. Karazhan dominates Deadwind Pass, built above a powerful meeting of ley lines. The tower was Guardian Medivh's stronghold, where he plotted to open the Dark Portal and bring ruin to Stormwind. During the First War, Lord Anduin Lothar and the young Khadgar led an expedition into the tower after Medivh's madness and possession came to light. They killed him there.

His death released fel taint across the pass and Duskwood. Karazhan remains an ominous ruin, and its unstable magic still leaks into the land. South of the main road, Deadwind ogres hold the territory around the Vice. Clad in foul rags and armed with jagged iron, they ambush anyone who ventures near the southern road. Reports say they serve a hidden master nearby.

Farther south, Morgan's Plot holds the skeletal remains of a hamlet that once served the tower. Ruins above ground and twisting cellars echo with wailing phantoms and restless shades, the dead left by Karazhan's unleashed sorcery.

zone:desolace.text:
Desolace. Across Desolace, centaur tribes fight for the plains as Horde, Alliance, and demonic cults press into the wastes. Gray earth, storm-dark skies, ancient ruins, and fallen beasts mark Kalimdor’s western coast. Storm-dark skies hang over Desolace, where gray earth lies broken and pools have turned yellow. Legend says Princess Theradras, an earth elemental, drained the land’s life to restore her form. Zaetar, son of Cenarius, came to subdue her, but became her mate instead. Their union brought the first centaur. Ashamed and enraged, the newborn centaur killed their father and spread across the plains, leaving the scarred waste travelers see today. Thousands of hooves thunder across Desolace as four centaur tribes fight outsiders and one another. The Kolkar roam the eastern cliffs, while the Magram keep crude yurts around brackish sinkholes. Farther south, the Gelkis live beyond rope bridges in deep ravines. The fanatical Maraudine guard the approach to Maraudon. Travelers crossing the wastes are often drawn into this old blood feud. Safe passage may mean fighting one tribe to win a wary parley with another. Beyond centaur lands, dangers gather along Desolace’s borders. The Burning Blade operates from Thunder Axe Fortress and Shadowbreak Ravine, summoning demons and satyrs whose fel fire threatens the region.

Naga creep onto the storm-lashed beaches of Ethel Rethor, while Darkspear trolls spear fish from the stilts of Shadowprey Village. High in the northern crags, the Alliance keeps watch from Nijel's Point. They fear Horde expansion and the demonic taint spreading from Mannoroc Coven.

zone:dunmorogh.text:
Dun Morogh. Dun Morogh is high snow country, the mountain home of the dwarves. The gnomes shelter here too, for they have lost their own home. But the snows are not safe. Troggs and Frostmane trolls prowl them, and so do the leper gnomes. The mountains rise between Searing Gorge in the south and the Wetlands in the north. Their snowmelt feeds the rivers of Khaz Modan, and copper and iron run in veins through the rock. Dwarven Mountaineers watch the narrow roads at the north and south gates. And beneath the tallest mountain lies Ironforge, the seat of King Magni Bronzebeard. Centuries ago, the dwarves drove the native Frostmane ice trolls up into the crags. So they made room for themselves, beside their gnome allies. The two peoples thrived in neighboring mountain halls, until the Third War. Then Gnomeregan fell.

Troggs invaded the gnomes' city, and radioactive gas ruined it. Its own defenders were twisted into leper gnomes. High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque led the survivors into exile, and now they live as guests in Ironforge. But the leper gnomes and the troggs spill out into Chill Breeze Valley. The Frostmane have grown bolder, with armed camps from Shimmer Ridge to Coldridge Valley. Troggs have clawed up from old fissures into Gol'Bolar Quarry, and the mines are in danger. Wendigos and wild boars roam the drifts, and the Dark Iron dwarves send in their spies. Toxic fallout spreads from the ruins of Gnomeregan. The Mountaineers struggle to keep order, from Kharanos to the border gates.

zone:durotar.text: Durotar. Durotar is red canyon country, where young orcs and Darkspear trolls prove themselves to the New Horde. Warchief Thrall founded this dry homeland after the Third War, and named it for his father, Durotan. The Southfury River and the Great Sea hem it in. Razor Hill and the warrior city of Orgrimmar rise from its rock. But quilboar tribes still hold out here, and so do stranded Alliance troops. Thrall chose this hard frontier on purpose. Here the orcs would earn an honest living by labor and grit, and not by conquest. The cracked red soil and the towering spires remind them of Draenor, before its ruin. Water is scarce and little of the land can be farmed, yet the Horde has embraced its stark grandeur. Durotar is proof that the orcs have forged their own destiny. The Horde holds Durotar, but keeping it is still a war. The Razormane quilboar, pushed out when the nation was founded, raid its farms from the western crags. In the south, what is left of Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's fleet still holds Tiragarde Keep, and refuses to surrender. Worse still, the demon cult of the Burning Blade lurks in hidden ravines and deep sea caves. It tempts young orcs back to fel power. On the southern coast lies Sen'jin Village, where the exiled Darkspear trolls gather under Master Gadrin. Their home was on the nearby Echo Isles. But the witch doctor Zalazane went mad, and with dark voodoo he enslaved his own kin. The Darkspear cannot take the islands back alone. They are counting on new warriors from the Valley of Trials, to break Zalazane's hold.

zone:duskwood.text:
Duskwood. In Duskwood, unending gloom hides the forest's sunlit past beneath a curse. Stormwind has abandoned its human inhabitants, who cling to survival in Darkshire under the Night Watch's protection. Ghouls, giant venomous spiders, raiding ogres, and savage, mysterious worgen roam the groves and haunted barrows. Duskwood once fed the Kingdom of Stormwind with rich farmland and prosperous settlements such as Grand Hamlet and Raven Hill. Its ruin began when Guardian Medivh fell at Karazhan during the First War. Waves of corrupted fel magic twisted the woodland into a gnarled, shadowy morass.

Spiders became terrible predators, and fleeing wolves spilled north into Elwynn Forest. Grand Hamlet became Darkshire, where townsfolk were left largely to fend for themselves after the royal garrison withdrew to defend the capital. Commander Althea Ebonlocke and her volunteer militia, the Night Watch, keep Darkshire alive. Lord Ello Ebonlocke tries to govern the crumbling settlement. Beyond the town's lantern-lit perimeter, danger fills the land. The restless dead raised by necromancer Morbent Fel stir in massive Raven Hill Cemetery. Vul'Gol ogres came from Deadwind Pass to claim the south, while Dark Riders stalk the crossroads in relentless search of the lost Scythe. Near Duskwood's center lies a deep, ancient crater untouched by the surrounding corruption: the Twilight Grove. An ancient Great Tree there holds a dormant portal into the Emerald Dream. Soft, ethereal twilight bathes this unearthly sanctuary in the dying land. Sleeping druidic energies watch over it.

zone:dustwallow.text:
Dustwallow Marsh. Across central Kalimdor, Dustwallow Marsh lies between the Barrens and the Great Sea. Underground springs feed its treacherous fens, where dangerous predators, covert faction skirmishes, and the black dragonflight all lurk. To the east, theramore isle is an Alliance fortress; to the northwest, Horde-allied Stonemaul ogres hold Brackenwall Village. Before the Great Sundering, Dustwallow was a high, grassy plain where herds roamed. The cataclysm shattered the valley and raised the water table, drowning the land in endless stagnant pools, mossy shallows, and choking mud.

Underground springs keep the marsh humid and submerged beneath thick fog. Crocolisks, raptors, and spiders haunt the fens. Crumbling causeways cross them, but jagged shallows and wandering bogs make every step beyond those roads perilous. Dustwallow stayed largely wild until after the Third War, when Lady Jaina Proudmoore led human refugees across the sea and founded the citadel of Theramore Isle on the eastern coast. Soon, Kul Tiran forces under Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore fought Thrall's fledgling Horde in bloody battles across the wetlands. The Admiral was defeated, and Theramore and Orgrimmar now keep an official armistice.

Tension still smolders. Theramore faces desertions and sabotage, while spies wage quiet, deadly conflicts across the fens.

zone:easternplaguelands.text:
Eastern Plaguelands. Scourge blight darkens the Eastern Plaguelands. Stratholme remains an undead stronghold, while the Scarlet Crusade fortifies the east. Light's Hope Chapel offers neutral refuge to those who fight back. Once called the Eastweald, the Eastern Plaguelands were Lordaeron's fertile heartland. Stratholme anchored the region, with prosperous towns like Darrowshire and Corin's Crossing nearby. During the Third War, Prince Arthas purged Stratholme after learning its grain had been laced with the Plague of Undeath.

After Lordaeron fell, Scourge magic spread unchecked. The soil turned brown and rotten. Ordinary plants warped into colossal mushrooms, and orange mist settled over the valleys. Stratholme is the Scourge's southern seat of power in Lordaeron. Baron Rivendare commands it under the direction of the lich Kel'Thuzad. In the southeast, the fanatical Scarlet Crusade has fortified Tyr's Hand and assaults Stratholme's scarlet strongholds.

The Crusade's hatred reaches beyond the undead to any living traveler who crosses its borders. Farther north, the Mossflayer forest trolls of Zul'Mashar wage isolated, desperate campaigns amid the wider conflict. Watch your footing in the Eastern Plaguelands. The neutral Argent Dawn keeps Light's Hope Chapel in the far east, where Alliance and Horde champions can find shelter, supplies, and flight routes. Beyond the chapel, ruined watchtowers mark Lordaeron's lost defenses: Crown Guard, Eastwall, Northpass, and Plaguewood.

zone:elwynn.text:
Elwynn Forest. Elwynn Forest is good green country, and Stormwind lives off its timber and gold, its fish and grain. It ought to be a peaceful place. But vermin, stray beasts and brigands roam the woods. So Northshire Abbey sends its recruits out to deal with them. The forest runs south from Stormwind's gates, all the way down to the Nazferiti River. It rains a good deal here, and the fields are the richer for it. Behind the fields grow thick hardwoods, and their timber goes to the capital. Carts roll up from Goldshire and the Eastvale Logging Camp, loaded with grain and livestock, lumber and raw copper. Elwynn breeds horses too, and knights and travelers all over the kingdom are glad to own a sturdy Evendale horse. But these are uneasy days. The Stormwind Army is busy far away, so the marshals and deputies must make do with recruits who have never been tested. Kobolds have overrun the Fargodeep and Jasperlode mines. Riverpaw gnolls prowl the southwestern borders, and murlocs have taken the shores of Stone Cairn Lake and Crystal Lake.

Even the wolves are newcomers. They fled the corruption across the river in Duskwood, and came over into Elwynn.

zone:felwood.text:
Felwood. Felwood remains in the grip of corruption between Ashenvale and Mount Hyjal. Once a paradise tended by night elves, it was poisoned by demonic magic during the Third War. Satyrs, twisted beasts, and ancients roam its depths as the Cenarion Circle and Alliance and Horde outposts work to cleanse it. Before the Third War, clear streams ran beneath singing birds, and ancient protectors guarded the peaceful groves. Then the dreadlord Tichondrius and the Burning Legion brought that peace to an end. Before their assault on Mount Hyjal, they used the Skull of Gul'dan to poison northern Kalimdor. Its sorcery blackened the forest floor and turned it to mire.

Illidan Stormrage later slew Tichondrius and consumed the artifact's essence. Yet the fel corruption remained. Treants and ancients rotted within, rivers boiled with bile, and the forest's beasts fell into cannibalistic madness. The work of healing Felwood is slow. On its southern border, the Cenarion Circle fights the blight from the Emerald Sanctuary. Its druids tend poisoned songflowers and night dragon bulbs, and give wanderers Cenarion beacons and cleansing salves.

The night elves hold Talonbranch Glade in the north, while the Horde keeps Bloodvenom Post. Both footholds stand amid a deadly wilderness where nature has turned against mortal flesh.

zone:feralas.text: Feralas. In Feralas, rainforest endures between Desolace, Thousand Needles, and the Veiled Sea. Mountain walls shelter an ancient wilderness of overgrown Kaldorei ruins and primordial beasts. Highborne remnants, Gordunni ogres, and rival Alliance and Horde outposts contend for its reaches. You enter a rainforest still green while Desolace and Thousand Needles lie dry nearby. Mountain ranges keep the wastes at bay, sheltering ancient growth beneath warm, misty air and towering waterfalls. Much of Kalimdor looked this way before the Great Sundering. Over the ages, jungle growth swallowed the monuments of the Kaldorei who once ruled here, hiding forgotten temples and pavilions beneath moss and ferns. At Feralas's heart, Eldre'Thalas lies in ruins, now called Dire Maul. The Kaldorei built the city at their empire's height, but the Gordunni ogres have defiled its vast stone courtyards. The clan spreads through the valley, pillaging sacred sites, fouling pristine groves, and driving wildlife to defend its territory. Whispers speak of Highborne remnants and powers trapped for ten thousand years in Dire Maul's sealed chambers. Alliance and Horde expeditions have pushed into the jungle, where every crossing brings danger. At Feathermoon Stronghold on Sardor Isle, General Shandris Feathermoon leads Sentinels against the ogres and advancing naga. Farther east, Camp Mojache anchors the Horde against aggressive Woodpaw gnolls, hostile Grimtotem tauren, and relentless ogres. Neither faction controls Feralas's wild interior.

zone:gnomeregan.text:
Gnomeregan. In Dun Morogh, Gnomeregan lies ruined and quarantined after the gnomes' desperate defense against troggs. Once their underground capital and greatest technological wonder, it now holds irradiated halls, mutated troggs, deranged leper gnomes, and rogue mechanical sentries. Its surviving people live as refugees in nearby Ironforge. Beneath Dun Morogh, Gnomeregan gathered gnomish invention, competitive craft, and politics under one roof. With help from the nearby dwarves of Ironforge, its people built a vast mechanical complex, powered by grinding engines and whirring gears.

Its intricate ventilation network took fifteen technicians working around the clock to keep fresh air moving. At Tinkers' Court, gnomes debated and competed as their capital grew into a marvel of industry. During the Second War, they sent the Alliance of Lordaeron siege engines, flying machines, and armaments. During the Third War, as the Scourge tore through Lordaeron, dwarven excavations at the ancient titan vault of Uldaman awakened primitive troggs beneath Dun Morogh. The creatures burrowed into Gnomeregan's lower foundations, and High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque led the defense.

As the city's defenses began to fail, Mekkatorque followed the counsel of his chief advisor, Mekgineer Thermaplugg. He ordered radioactive waste tanks vented into the lower levels to eradicate the invaders. The toxic gas spread beyond control. Nearly eighty percent of the gnomish population died within days.

zone:hallofthanes.text: Hall of Thanes. Alliance defenders now seek a way into the Hall of Thanes, deep beneath Ironforge. Its old vaults hold dwarven relics, and danger has reached those depths. Hammers ring in Ironforge's Great Forge, but forgotten halls run deeper beneath the stone. The Hall of Thanes lies in those ancient reaches, tied to dwarven bloodlines and relics of stonecraft. Now Alliance champions must enter its shadowed vaults and guard the depths. The route into the Hall of Thanes is hidden from Ironforge's everyday travelers. Its corridors have been sealed or concealed. To find a way through, recover an Underground Map and use forgotten charts to navigate the deeper tunnels to the entrance.

zone:hillsbrad.text:
Hillsbrad Foothills. In Hillsbrad Foothills, green fields still divide two forces at war. Southshore's humans and the Forsaken at Tarren Mill clash across the pastures, making the region a battleground for Alliance and Horde armies. Hillsbrad Foothills still holds green fields while blight consumes much of northern Lordaeron. Its pastures, pine groves, and working farms recall the kingdom before the Third War. Armed patrols, rogue mercenaries, and scavenger beasts cross the fields and roads. Once Lordaeron's breadbasket, Hillsbrad is now one of its most contested borderlands. Southshore stands on the southern coast, held by human refugees and soldiers loyal to the Alliance. North of it, Tarren Mill was once a quiet human farming hamlet. The Scourge destroyed it, and the Forsaken fortified it as their southernmost garrison. Between them, open ground has become a relentless killing ground, where Alliance and Horde champions skirmish for control of Hillsbrad. Hillsbrad's violence reaches back to the Second War. Its coast and hills saw the first great clashes between the Grand Alliance and the Old Horde. Later, Durnholde Keep held the internment camp where Thrall was raised before leading the orcish rebellion. Now the ruined keep belongs to the Syndicate, displaced human nobles turned bandits.

Coastal murlocs, hostile gnolls, and the shadowed dead on Purgation Isle leave no corner of the hills secure.

zone:hinterlands.text:
The Hinterlands. The Hinterlands still bear the Amani's old claims, while Wildhammer dwarves hold Aerie Peak. Forest trolls keep their ruined temples, and the Revantusk have made a village on the eastern coast. The Amani forest trolls ruled the Hinterlands long before humans or dwarves came to northern Lordaeron. Their defeat in the ancient Troll Wars broke the empire into separate tribes. Centuries later, the War of the Three Hammers drove the Wildhammer dwarves from Grim Batol.

They migrated north and settled above ground at Aerie Peak. There, they tamed native gryphons and kept their shamanic traditions as they built a great stronghold in the heights. The forest trolls saw them as squatters on ancestral land. Skirmishes and raids have kept the feud alive ever since. Three forest troll tribes occupy the dense woods and ruined temples. The strongest are the brutal Vilebranch, who hold the terraced temple city of Jintha'Alor and the towering Altar of Zul. Farther south, the weaker Witherbark cling to Shadra'Alor and Hiri'Watha.

The nomadic Revantusk were long scorned by their cousins and had no true home. After the Third War, they made a treaty with Thrall's New Horde. With aid from orcs and Forsaken, they founded Revantusk Village on the eastern sea cliffs and claimed a coastal stronghold of their own.

zone:ironforge.text:
Ironforge. Ironforge is carved into the heart of a mountain, in the snows of Dun Morogh. It is the ancient capital of the Bronzebeard dwarves, and one of the Alliance's strongest bulwarks. At its center burns the Great Forge. Here King Magni Bronzebeard rules, and now his halls also shelter the gnomes who lost Gnomeregan. Twenty-five centuries ago, the first dwarves awoke in Uldaman. Westward they journeyed, into the jagged peaks of Dun Morogh, and delved into the tallest mountain. There they raised a shrine to their maker, the titan Khaz'goroth, and beside it the Great Forge. And ever since, the city has grown outward in rings around that fiery hearth.

No city above the ground is like it. Ironforge lies wholly beneath stone, warmed by roaring hearths and by rivers of molten rock. Its fortified gates and deep halls have held through centuries of war. For generations, three dwarven clans shared the mountain. The Bronzebeards lived beside the Wildhammers and the Dark Irons. When High King Modimus Anvilmar died, a bitter civil war broke out for rule of Ironforge. The Bronzebeards won it, and drove their rivals out.

Then Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan led the Dark Irons back for vengeance. His siege reached the very heart of Ironforge, before the Bronzebeards threw it back. In the south, by mischance, Thaurissan then summoned Ragnaros the Firelord. The Firelord's coming shattered the Redridge Mountains, and doomed Thaurissan's own host. Ever since, the Bronzebeards have held Ironforge unchallenged. In the Second War, the Bleeding Hollow clan overran much of Khaz Modan. But Ironforge held firm behind its sealed gates, until the Alliance of Lordaeron broke the siege. For that debt of honor, King Magni Bronzebeard pledged Ironforge to the Alliance forever. He stood by it even when Gilneas and Quel'Thalas walked away. In the Third War, Magni mourned his brother Muradin, lost in Northrend. When Gnomeregan fell, the king opened his gates to thousands of gnome refugees. Under High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque, they carved out Tinker Town within the stone city. And the Deeprun Tram now runs beneath the earth, straight to Stormwind. So Ironforge has become a crossroads of dwarven steel and gnomish invention.

zone:lochmodan.text: Loch Modan. Loch Modan's great lake stands above the Wetlands, held back by the Stonewrought Dam. Around Thelsamar, troggs threaten the southern valleys, kobolds work the mines, and ogres hold the northeast highlands. Loch Modan's lake fills a green valley east of Dun Morogh. Pines and birches climb toward rugged peaks, and the Stonewrought Dam spans the northern rim. The dwarven town of Thelsamar draws mountaineers, hunters, and miners. Copper and tin run through the surrounding hills. Broken catapults and ballistae on the lake bed recall the Second War. The orcish Horde occupied Loch Modan then, until the dwarves drove them out. More recently, dwarven excavations opened underground chambers and released savage troggs. Their tribes, led by chieftains, overran the southern canyons of Stonesplinter Valley and the Valley of Kings. The Ironforge Mountaineers fight to defend the trade routes.

zone:moonglade.text: Moonglade. In Moonglade, druids of the Cenarion Circle gather beneath an endless twilight. The valley in northern Kalimdor shelters night elf and tauren druids, while travelers on foot brave Timbermaw Hold to reach it. Moonglade lies among the mountains north of Felwood and Winterspring. Beneath Elune's moon, twilight lingers over Lake Elune'ara, at the heart of a valley sacred since kaldorei civilization began. The Burning Legion left the glade untouched in both its ancient invasions and the recent Third War, held back by Cenarius and his offspring. Keeper Remulos watches over Moonglade now, guarding nature's balance in a refuge where factional conflict has no place. Malfurion Stormrage founded the Cenarion Circle millennia ago, and Moonglade remains its headquarters. In lakeside Nighthaven, druids learn from ancient traditions. After the Third War, the Circle welcomed tauren into its ranks, following Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem's teachings. Here, Alliance and Horde loyalties are set aside. Armed sentries keep the peace, and members who turn to violence face swift justice.

zone:mulgore.text:
Mulgore. Below the Stonetalon Mountains lies Mulgore, the green and sheltered homeland of the tauren. Grasslands and rolling plains spread between its tall plateaus, and high mountain walls ring it round. It is the heart of the united tribes, and they watch over it from Thunder Bluff. For generations, the tauren lived as nomads, hunted across the plains by centaur warbands. Their fortune turned when High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof met Thrall and his orcs. They shared ideals of honor, shamanism and strength, so the tauren joined the young Horde. With the orcs' help, Cairne broke the centaur's grip and led his people into Mulgore. Here they built lasting homes for the first time in centuries, and crowned the northern mesas with their capital. To come of age in Mulgore, young tauren must answer the call of the Great Hunt and honor the Earthmother. Their training begins at Camp Narache, under Chief Hawkwind. From there they go down to Bloodhoof Village, and take up the Rites of the Earthmother. They learn to speak with the ancestral spirits and to forage the native herbs. And they learn to respect the herds of kodos and tallstriders that sustain their people. For all its calm, Mulgore is threatened on every side. Displaced quilboar have dug in at Brambleblade Ravine, and they have defiled the sacred burial grounds of Red Rocks. In the mountains, Windfury harpies prey on the wild game, and Palemane gnolls strike from hidden caves.

And outsiders have come to profit from the land. The goblins of the Venture Company are fouling the sacred wells, and quarrying the eastern hills. Dwarven explorers from Bael Modan have opened the Bael'dun Digsite. There they dig for ancient titan relics, over the tauren's protests.

zone:orgrimmar.text:
Orgrimmar. Out of the red canyons of northern Durotar rises Orgrimmar, stronghold of the orcs. It is the heart of the New Horde. Trolls, tauren and Forsaken allies have found shelter within its walls. The orcs came here looking for a home. After the Third War, Warchief Thrall led them to the dry coasts of Kalimdor. There they would be free at last, of demon taint and of human chains. He named the land Durotar, after his father. And he named the city for Orgrim Doomhammer, the mentor he had lost.

The stronghold was raised with blood and sweat. Tauren stood with the orcs, and Darkspear trolls, and goblin engineers. The Champion Rexxar stood with them too. Together they drove back the centaurs, the harpies and the fierce thunder lizards of the canyons. Rugged mountains ring the city. They keep out both foreign foes and the razor-winds of Durotar. Within, the rock opens into hollows, and each valley has its own part in the life of the Horde.

In the Valley of Strength stands the gatehouse. From it a road runs deeper in, to the market of the Drag. Tauren druids and shaman gather by the pools in the Valley of Wisdom. And in the Valley of Spirits, the shadow hunters and witch doctors of the Darkspear dwell among their pavilions on stilts.

zone:ragefire.text: Ragefire Chasm. Beneath Orgrimmar, troggs and a demonic cult threaten the young Horde. The Searing Blade plots in volcanic caverns below the Cleft of Shadow, with the capital above. Ragefire troggs burst from deep beneath Orgrimmar into winding volcanic corridors and lava pits. As orcish builders raise their new home above, the troggs grow more aggressive. Magatha Grimtotem sends Maur Grimtotem to speak for Thunder Bluff, but the troggs slaughter him. They yield only to force. The Searing Blade, a demonic cult, poses a greater danger than the troggs. Loyal to the Shadow Council, its fanatics plot the young Horde's ruin in caverns beside streams of magma. Jergosh the Invoker, a cunning warlock, leads with Bazzalan, a satyr, and Taragaman the Hungerer, a vicious felguard. Taragaman presides over an altar in the lava lake.

zone:razorfenkraul.text: Razorfen Kraul. In the far south of the Barrens, quilboar defend the sacred brambles of Razorfen Kraul. They honor the thickets as the resting place of their ancestor, Agamaggan, while Charlga Razorflank’s rule threatens the region. Ten thousand years ago, Agamaggan fought the Burning Legion in the War of the Ancients. The colossal wild god fell, but his sacrifice preserved life on Azeroth. Legends tell that thorn-covered vines rose wherever his blood entered the earth, forming thick defenses across the southern plains. The quilboar honor Agamaggan as their divine ancestor and claim the thickets as holy ground. The greatest of them became the Razorfen.

zone:redridge.text: Redridge Mountains. Redridge Mountains now face attacks from Shadowhide gnolls and Blackrock orcs of the Dark Horde. Rushing rivers run through wooded slopes around Lake Everstill, while Lakeshire holds the line with wandering mercenaries as Stormwind’s forces contend with strife at home. Redridge once stood among the kingdom’s most peaceful regions. Its forests supplied Stormwind with timber, while its waters and fields gave the kingdom fish and crops. Now Lakeshire is fortified against repeated attacks. Stonewatch Keep, once a proud stronghold of the kingdom, has fallen to renegade Blackrock orcs. Their hold cuts off roads and threatens the eastern valleys. These peaks form part of the spine that runs down the subcontinent of Azeroth. Centuries ago, the range stretched much farther north. Then the Dark Iron clan accidentally summoned the Firelord Ragnaros, and the earth split open to form the fiery crater of Blackrock Mountain. The cataclysm severed the northern peaks into the ash-choked Burning Steppes. Only the southern Redridge valleys remain lush and green, exposed to attacks from the slopes above. Magistrate Solomon and Marshal Marris plead for reinforcements, but Stormwind’s regency council leaves Lakeshire to fend for itself. Appeals to Sentinel Hill and Darkshire bring no aid; both settlements are crippled by crises of their own. With no reinforcements in sight, local magistrates hire any capable sellsword willing to brave the Lakeridge Highway, clear the gnoll camps, and push back the danger across Lake Everstill.

zone:riverglades.text: Riverglades. In Riverglades, human loyalists and Horde outposts still contest a valley east of the Badlands and Burning Steppes. Stormwind once claimed the region, but the Old Horde overran it in the First War. The Redridge Mountains lie southwest, the Swamp of Sorrows south, and Tanaris across the sea. Before the First War, Riverglades belonged to the Kingdom of Stormwind. Then the Old Horde swept through. Orcs sacked Sunnyglade but spared its mage tower to study human sorcery. They enslaved the townsfolk who survived. Stormwind soldiers tried to free the captives and rebuild, but the kingdom judged the valley lost and sent its strength to defend the core homelands. For years, the crown gave Riverglades little formal support. Stormwind's leaders left Riverglades behind, yet its human defenders never fully surrendered their homeland. Knight Commander Demar Brant leads the remaining loyalists of the legendary brotherhood of the horse. They hold farholde keep against the wilderness and hostile invaders. Nearby, the modern Horde keeps a strong presence at outposts such as rog'mar and bolder'ok. The old struggle over the glades continues. Riverglades follows the coast of the Forbidding Sea, among mountains and winding waterways. You can cross west through Blackrock Pass to the Burning Steppes, or travel southwest through Redridge Pass to the Redridge Mountains. South lies the Swamp of Sorrows. To the northwest, trails pass Twilight's Shroud into the Badlands. At powderfuse port, you can take a boat across the sea to steamwheedle port in Tanaris.

zone:ruinsoflordaeron.text:
Ruins of Lordaeron. Above Undercity, the Ruins of Lordaeron still shelter horrors from the fallen capital. Prince Arthas and the Scourge brought the human kingdom to ruin during the Third War. Now the Alliance and Horde venture across the surface to reclaim relics of the past or purge its threats. Capital City once held the crown of the Eastern Kingdoms. King Terenas Menethil II sat on its throne, and human civilization stood at its heart. When Prince Arthas returned from Northrend, he killed his father in the throne room and unleashed the undead upon the people.

The Forsaken now dwell in the catacombs below, in Undercity. Above them, the surface remains a forsaken twilight zone. Broken arches and weed-choked cobbles shelter feral beasts such as Witherfang and deranged remnants of the past. Restless dead are not the only danger in the ruined grounds. Apothecaries and sinister figures such as viktor the vile test new plagues in the shadows, while twisted experiments such as the abandoned roam freely.

Wrathful spirits such as rath'mael and cursed retainers such as The Baron haunt the collapsed halls, trapped in endless torment. They strike at any living or undead trespasser who crosses their path.

zone:scarlet.text:
Scarlet Monastery. In the northeastern hills of Tirisfal Glades, Scarlet Monastery shelters the Scarlet Crusade behind fortified walls. Once a peaceful sanctuary and a center of learning for the Church of the Holy Light, it now holds four wings where zealots train, torture captives, and wage war on outsiders. Before the Third War, the Scarlet Monastery was a proud seat of Lordaeron's priesthood, devoted to learning and enlightenment. Then the Scourge devastated the land. The surviving crusaders cleared the halls of undead and spiders, and made the archives and courtyards a fortified garrison.

Grief and fear hardened into suspicion. The Scarlet Crusade came to see every outsider as a carrier of the plague, living or undead, human or otherwise. In their eyes, such foes must be cleansed with fire. Beyond the Grand Vestibule lie four wings. In the Graveyard, fallen crusaders rise as undead abominations, while torturers force confessions from prisoners. The Library holds theological and historical works, guarded by renegade mage Arcanist Doan and his hounds.

In the Armory, weaponmasters such as Herod train recruits to fight as disciplined warriors. Deep within the stronghold lies the Cathedral, the Crusade's heart. There, its leaders direct their campaign across the blighted north.

zone:searinggorge.text:
Searing Gorge. In Searing Gorge, the Dark Iron clan works a land once joined to the green Redridge Mountains. Ragnaros the Firelord scorched it when he was summoned over two centuries ago. Now the Thorium Brotherhood watches the clan's slave mines in the Cauldron. Before the War of the Three Hammers, Searing Gorge was a green, rolling part of the Redridge chain. That land was lost over two hundred and thirty years ago. Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan summoned Ragnaros from deep beneath the world, hoping to turn defeat into victory. The Firelord tore the earth apart, raised Blackrock Mountain and reduced the great Dark Iron city of Thaurissan to smoking ruins. Ash, sulfur and volcanic glass covered the northern valley. After their old capital fell, the Dark Iron dwarves seized the gorge for the materials their war machine needed. At the valley's heart, the Cauldron cuts deep into the stone as a vast open-pit excavation. In its lower reaches, the Slag Pit forms a harsh underground mining complex.

Dark Iron overseers and lumbering war golems force captured enemies into slave labor, hauling iron, mithril and rare Dark Iron ore from burning rock. Lava surges and roaming beasts threaten the miners at every turn. Thorium Point crowns the northern crags above the excavation. The Thorium Brotherhood holds this fortified outpost, after splitting from its kin in Blackrock Mountain. Its master craftsmen offer travelers neutral shelter in return for undermining Dark Iron operations or bringing rare smelting components.

Access to the gorge remains tightly controlled. The Alliance bars Stonewrought Pass toward Loch Modan with heavy iron gates, while Horde expeditions from nearby Kargath have cut a narrow trail through the eastern badlands to scout the region.

zone:shadowfang.text:
Shadowfang Keep. In southern Silverpine, Shadowfang Keep shelters Archmage Arugal and the worgen he summoned. The old Silverlaine estate is overrun by feral beasts and haunted by its slaughtered defenders. Nearby Pyrewood Village remains bound to a horrifying curse. Shadowfang Keep once belonged to the Silverlaine family, with pious Commander Springvale charged to defend it. During the Third War, the Scourge swept through Lordaeron, and Dalaran's wizards fell in droves. Desperate to stem the dead, Archmage Arugal defied the Kirin Tor leadership and used the research of the wizard Ur.

He summoned worgen from beyond this world to turn the tide. The beasts savaged the undead, then slipped beyond mortal control and stormed southern Silverpine. Baron Silverlaine and his court were massacred, doomed to haunt the stone halls beside the monsters that overran their home. Guilt and madness drove Arugal behind the blood-stained battlements. He called the ravenous wolf-men his beloved children and gave the castle the name Shadowfang Keep. Lupine packs and shadowy hounds thrive in its stone roosts under trainers such as Wolf Master Nandos. Arugal's massive lupine beast, Fenrus the Devourer, watches over them.

The curse reached beyond the walls. Nearby Pyrewood Village remains trapped in a horrifying cycle: its people walk as men by day, then hunt as ravenous worgen beneath the moon. They are bound to the mad archmage on the heights above.

zone:shendralas.text: Shen'dralas. Centaur, outcasts, and quilboar contest Shen'dralas, south east of desolace. Ancient ruins rise among its crags, between Feralas and Mulgore. Shen'dralas lies in the heights south east of desolace, between Mulgore and Feralas. Its craggy passes and hidden enclaves shelter groups struggling to survive far from the great faction capitals. At Evenshade Overlook, some watch from secluded heights. At Outcast Hideaway, others seek refuge where they can be forgotten. Ancient ruins recall the highborne legacy behind Shen'dralas's name, yet the land is far from peaceful. Centaur feuds spill across the Magram Front, keeping old bloodshed alive along the borders. Bristleback quilboar hold fortified ground at Bristleback Retreat. Travelers find contested territory in the ravines. The valley of bones leads north-west toward Desolace and offers the main overland route into Shen'dralas. Sun and wind have bleached the passage. Its bones recall the violent struggles that still sweep through these crags.

zone:silithus.text:
Silithus. Silithus lies beneath spreading silithid swarms, watched by the Cenarion Circle. The desert holds the ancient ruins of Ahn'Qiraj, sealed behind the Scarab Wall a thousand years ago. Druids guard against the swarms and Twilight's Hammer cultists. You enter Silithus from Un'Goro Crater through a broad, rocky pass in its northwest corner. Jungle gives way to dunes, jagged stone, and towering hives. Water is scarce, and the wind carries the hum of insect wings across the sand. Near the desert's center, Cenarion Hold offers shelter to travelers, researchers, and warriors. The Cenarion Circle keeps this outpost as the only refuge in the hostile wastes. A thousand years ago, night elves and the great dragonflights fought desperately to drive back the Qiraji in the War of the Shifting Sands. The Qiraji were an insectoid empire born from the ancient Aqiri civilization.

When victory proved beyond reach, the defenders sealed the swarms inside their stronghold with the Scarab Wall and enchanted Scarab Dais. The gates held, but silithids burrowed through tunnels below and formed vast colonies across the desert, including Hive'Ashi, Hive'Zora, and Hive'Regal. Twilight's Hammer has fortified several outposts in Silithus. Its cultists summon elemental terrors and worship the dark power beneath Ahn'Qiraj. Cenarion Circle observers watch the silithid colonies spread and keep guard against the ancient threat behind the Scarab Wall.

zone:silverpine.text:
Silverpine Forest. Forsaken patrols hold Silverpine Forest, where rival forces threaten the woods along Lordaeron’s western coast. The Scourge’s plague scars the forest, and worgen, diseased gnolls, and hostile human enclaves endanger travelers. Silverpine Forest stretches between Tirisfal Glades and the sealed Greymane Wall. Once a lush wonder of Lordaeron, it has withered since the Third War. Ghostly fog drifts among dying, silver-barked pines, while ruined farmsteads lie abandoned to the wilderness.

Tirisfal Glades borders the forest to the north, and Lordamere Lake runs along its eastern shore. To the south, the Greymane Wall shuts Gilneas away from the chaos beyond. The Forsaken hold their central outpost at the Sepulcher, struggling to secure the woods from enemies on every side.

zone:stockade.text: The Stockade. Violent rebellion has seized The Stockade beneath Stormwind's canal district near the Mage Quarter. Built as a high-security prison for cutthroats, political insurgents, and captured enemies of state, it now holds dangerous prisoners in anarchy. Warden Thelwater is driven back to the entrance and seeks help before the riot reaches the capital. Beneath Stormwind's canals, the Stockade has become a war zone. When the regular army marched to distant fronts, understaffed prison guards relied on inexperienced youths, including fourteen-year-old recruits. They could not keep order. The inmates launched a bloody, coordinated rebellion, tore their wool blankets into gang scarves, and cut down the remaining guards. Warden Thelwater barely holds the entrance while convicts control the cells, hallways, and holding blocks.

zone:stonetalon.text:
Stonetalon Mountains. In Stonetalon Mountains, sacred heights face smoke, felled forests, and ruined earth. Night elves and tauren revere the range, while tensions simmer along its borders. Stonetalon Mountains rise from central Kalimdor beneath the Ill Winds. Moisture from the western seas brings sudden downpours, slicking the sandstone trails. Fierce gusts scour the lower valleys, blinding travelers with grit and sometimes hurling the careless from cliffs.

Higher ridges bear evergreen forests around Stonetalon Peak. Night elves tend ancestral barrows and glades there. They also watch sacred wyvern and hippogryph roosts along Mirkfallon Lake. The Venture Company has broken the range's quiet with logging camps and strip mines in Windshear Crag. Aided by Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle, the deranged leper gnome, the goblins have felled old-growth timber and filled the skies with furnace smoke. Their industrial sludge fouls the mountain runoff.

Local shamans from Orgrimmar answered the mountain spirits' cries. Small Alliance camps nearby also resist the defilers and try to protect the highlands that remain. South lies the Charred Vale, once a blossoming wilderness and now an ash-covered wasteland. Rogue fire elementals, black dragonspawn, and harpies fill its ruins. During the Third War, the Horde and Alliance forged an uneasy truce in these peaks under the mysterious Oracle's guidance.

Relations have since frayed. Renegade Grimtotem tauren hold seized encampments, while Darkspear trolls in Malaka'jin clash with Alliance forces pressing out from the Barrens and Ashenvale.

zone:stormwind.text:
Stormwind City. White-walled Stormwind is the greatest haven of men, and the heart of the Alliance. Yet its king is lost. The crown now rests on a boy of ten. Stormwind is old. More than a thousand years ago, the descendants of the Arathi founded it. For long generations it flourished, a realm that needed no one's help. Then the Horde came through the Dark Portal. The southern continent was laid waste, and in the First War the city was razed.

Its survivors followed Sir Anduin Lothar north, across the Great Sea to Lordaeron. When the Horde fell in the Second War, King Terenas Menethil II and the Alliance paid for Stormwind to rise again. The Stonemasons Guild raised it anew in polished white stone, with canals running through its boroughs. But the white stone hides a troubled house. The House of Nobles quarreled with the Stonemasons Guild over wages, and the quarrel left the kingdom crippled by debt. The guild's workers rose in riot. They were driven from the very city they had built.

Then King Varian Wrynn vanished on his way to a summit. Lest panic spread, the crown passed to his son Prince Anduin Wrynn. He is ten years old. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon rules now as Regent and commander of the army. And at his side stands the royal advisor, Lady Katrana Prestor. With Lordaeron overrun by the Scourge, men look to Stormwind above every other city. The faithful gather at the Cathedral of Light. And in the Valley of Heroes, tall statues honor the Sons of Lothar. They passed beyond the Dark Portal, and were seen no more.

zone:stranglethorn.text: Stranglethorn Vale. Trolls, goblins, pirates, and soldiers contest Stranglethorn Vale. South of Duskwood, the old Gurubashi heartland has become a maze of ruins, beasts, and rival camps. Zul'Gurub once ruled the vale as the Gurubashi Empire's capital. That rule ended when radical priests summoned Hakkar the Soulflayer, and civil war tore through the region. The Zandalari crushed the blood god's uprising, but the empire never recovered. Now successor factions fight across the jungle. The Bloodscalp hold the northwest, while the Skullsplitter occupy the east. Both tribes slaughter outsiders as they fight to reclaim their ancestral home. Booty Bay fills the vale's southern tip with trade and sea traffic. The Steamwheedle Cartel carved out the port, and the Blackwater Raiders run it under Baron Revilgaz. Bloodsail Buccaneers anchored along the coast keep the port under constant threat. Farther inland, the Venture Company cuts timber and mines the hills for rare singing crystals. Rival powers meet across the vale's dangerous borderland. The Horde holds Grom'gol Base Camp on the western coast, and goblin zeppelins link it to Durotar and Tirisfal Glades. Alliance loyalists at the Rebel Camp hunt for the rogue Colonel Kurzen. In the thick jungle, famed hunter Hemet Nesingwary leads big-game expeditions. Wanderers drawn to his hunts face prowling panthers, enormous apes, and enemy soldiers.

zone:swampofsorrows.text:
Swamp of Sorrows. Green dragonspawn guard the drowned Temple of Atal'Hakkar beneath the Pool of Tears. Between Deadwind Pass and the Blasted Lands, this salt-crusted mire holds dangerous wildlife and the Horde garrison at Stonard. The Alliance has no safe haven here. The Swamp of Sorrows was once the northern half of the vast Black Morass. After the Gurubashi Empire shattered, fanatical Atal'ai trolls fled into the mire and built the Temple of Atal'Hakkar. They meant to summon Hakkar the Soulflayer, their bloodthirsty loa. The Aspect Ysera sensed the danger and drowned the cursed pyramid beneath the Pool of Tears. Green dragonflight guardians led by Eranikus were set to watch over it.

Later, the Dark Portal's cataclysm scorched the southern morass into the Blasted Lands. The northern fen took its sorrowful name. Stonard is the swamp's main foothold for settled folk. First established during the First War alongside Rockard and Kyross, both now ruined, it was rebuilt under Thrall as the Horde's southernmost staging ground in the Eastern Kingdoms.

Strange wanderers cross the fen beyond its palisades. Draenei stranded on Azeroth grew homesick and mad, becoming feral Lost Ones. At the Harborage, a small enclave of lucid Broken exiles remains wary, yet willing to trade peacefully with travelers. Predators make every crossing of the Swamp of Sorrows dangerous. Deep bogs conceal lunging crocolisks, venomous spiders, prowling swamp jaguars, and bog beasts coated in marsh debris. Vicious murlocs crawl through coastal caverns and along the Misty Reed Strand.

Salt-laden tides creep inland and crust rotten logs with brine. Farther east, aggressive elite dragonspawn guard the approaches to the Sunken Temple in Sorrowmurk. They attack anyone who strays near their vigil.

zone:tanaris.text:
Tanaris. In Tanaris, goblins trade beneath a fierce sun as dangers stir in the sands. Gadgetzan welcomes both the Alliance and the Horde, while Sandfury trolls, silithid, and ancient powers hold the dunes beyond. Tanaris lies beneath a fierce sun, and sand covers much of the land. Within Zul'Farrak's walls, the Sandfury trolls guard their isolated home. Hyenas, basilisks, and scorpids roam the desert floor. Tunnels wind beneath the hot earth. Close to the goblins' island homeland of Kezan, Tanaris has become a trading ground for the Steamwheedle Cartel. From walled Gadgetzan to the docks of steamwheedle port, the goblins welcome coin from the Alliance and the Horde alike. Bruisers keep the peace, yet Southsea Freebooters still harass ships and dig sites along the coast. Tanaris holds powers older than mortal empires. In the east, the Caverns of Time belong to Nozdormu and the bronze dragonflight. Their drakes sometimes ride the desert thermals.

Farther south, massive stone gates mark the titan complex of Uldum. Silithid swarms burrow outward from nests such as the Gaping Chasm and the Noxious Lair.

zone:teldrassil.text:
Teldrassil. Off Kalimdor's northwest shore rises Teldrassil, the World Tree, and in its crown lies Darnassus. The druids raised it after the Third War. Yet its growing is troubled. Vast are the limbs of Teldrassil, and far beneath them lies the Veiled Sea. Upon its boughs are hills and ancient glades, and misty lakes. Its rivers are fed by the morning dew. At the western edge stands Darnassus, city of the kaldorei.

Far below, at the foot of the trunk, lies Rut'theran Village. It is the island's harbor. And a gateway of enchantment joins it to the crown. In the Third War, Nordrassil was sacrificed. Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage passed into the Emerald Dream. In his absence, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm went before the Circle of Ancients. He prevailed upon them to grow another tree in its place. For he hoped to win back the undying life the kaldorei had lost.

But Nozdormu and the Dragon Aspects judged it a work of pride. They withheld their blessing. And so Teldrassil grew unwarded. With it grew flaws not of nature.

zone:thousandneedles.text:
Thousand Needles. In southern Kalimdor, Thousand Needles stands over a dry canyon of sandstone pillars. Tauren hold the mesas, while gnomes and goblins race rocket cars across the Shimmering Flats. Before the Great Sundering, inland waterways fed a lush river canyon that ran toward the sea. The cataclysm shattered ancient Kalimdor, raised the riverbed above the water table, and changed the river's course. Dry stone and sandstone spires remain. Dozens of slender, cylindrical columns rise from the canyon floor like a forest turned to stone.

Tauren built villages atop the columns and joined the peaks with precarious rope bridges. They sought escape from hostile centaur marauders patrolling the shadow-draped floor below. Life atop the needle-like spires is far from peaceful. At Freewind Post, tauren loyal to the Horde face predatory wind serpents and wyverns from Highperch, and treacherous kin of the militant Grimtotem clan, entrenched at Darkcloud Pinnacle. Cliffwatcher Longhorn directs the plateau's defense. He seeks bold fighters to strike Grimtotem agitators and secure the fragile bridges between peaks.

To the north, enormous mechanical winches at the Great Lift carry travelers down from the southern Barrens. Crossing the canyon floor remains a deadly gamble. To the southeast, the canyon walls open onto the Shimmering Flats, an enormous dried-up salt pan below sea level. Gnomes and goblins keep an uneasy neutrality around the Mirage Raceway in this harsh, blinding expanse. Rival engineers Pozzik and Fizzle Brassbolts race experimental rocket cars across the hard salt, each seeking to prove their race's technological superiority.

The pit stop draws scoundrels, swindlers like Kravel Koalbeard, and hunters pursuing the hardy scorpions, turtles, and basilisks that roam the searing basin.

zone:thunderbluff.text:
Thunder Bluff. High above the grasslands of Mulgore, Thunder Bluff rises on windswept red mesas. It is the capital of the tauren, and the heart of their spirit, their culture and their trade. Swaying rope bridges and wooden lifts join its heights. Safe from the centaur marauders, it is a place of peace for travelers from all over Kalimdor. For countless generations, the tauren wandered Kalimdor, fighting the centaur for their very survival. That age ended in the Third War, when High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof joined forces with Warchief Thrall. Together the orcs and tauren broke the centaur's assaults, and won the pastures of Mulgore. Then Cairne led the allied tribes up onto these bastions of stone, and founded Thunder Bluff. It was the first lasting home the united tribes had known in centuries. The central bluffs hold the markets, the bank and the inn, and a towering roost for the wind riders. Three more mesas branch out across the abyss, each with its own calling. Scouts and trackers live on Hunter Rise. The lorekeepers live on Elder Rise, with the Cenarion Circle under Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem.

And Spirit Rise is given to the spirits. There dwell the shaman and the priests. Deep beneath them lie the caverns called the Pools of Vision.

zone:tirisfal.text: Tirisfal Glades. Tirisfal Glades, in the north of Lordaeron, is home to Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and her Forsaken. Under blighted skies, fallen manors and dormant crypts surround their vast capital beneath the earth, the Undercity. The mindless Scourge hem them in, and so do the zealots of the Scarlet Crusade. Here the free-willed dead fight to survive. Tirisfal was once the fertile cradle of humanity, before the Lich King's plague withered its people. Now the sun rarely breaks through the gloom, over dying woods and cold coastal hills. Old farmsteads like the Agamand Mills still stand, but most of their masters lie in mass graves or walk as restless dead. Yet a dark resilience holds on in towns like Brill. And in Deathknell, the newly awakened Forsaken learn to endure their second life. Now Lady Sylvanas rules the region from beneath the Ruins of Lordaeron, yet her people are beset on every side. Scourge thralls still infest the hollows, the fields and the crumbling crypts, bound wholly to the Frozen Throne in Northrend. To the east, the Scarlet Crusade holds northern Tirisfal, from its stronghold at the Scarlet Monastery. Sworn to destroy every undead creature, its patrols wage constant guerrilla war on Forsaken scouts and travelers. Older than any human crown is the story of the Glades. Of old, high elven exiles sought to settle in these woods. But shadowy powers deep beneath the earth began to drive them mad, and they passed on into the north. Centuries later, the secret Council of Tirisfal chose these shadowed groves. Here it empowered its solitary Guardians, who shielded Azeroth from the demons.

zone:undercity.text:
Undercity. Beneath the shattered ruins of Lordaeron's capital lies the Undercity, the dark stronghold of the Forsaken. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner took it from the Scourge, and made it a sanctuary no enemy can breach. Today it is the seat of Forsaken power. And it is the Horde's great bastion, in the north of the Eastern Kingdoms. Long before the plague, the catacombs and sewers beneath the palace were already called the Undercity. Nobles lay entombed there, beside the poorest people of the realm. And there lay the kingdom's deepest prisons. Even Orgrim Doomhammer, the former Warchief, was held in them before he escaped.

In the Third War, Arthas Menethil murdered King Terenas, and laid waste to the capital. Then the prince set his undead servants to dig. They widened the old passages into a fortified seat of Scourge rule. But the Scourge never saw their dark capital finished. When the Lich King's power waned, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner broke free of his will, and took thousands of undead with her. She ambushed Arthas, and he fled back to Northrend.
